q: What is Windows PE (Windows Preinstallation Environment) most commonly used for?
options: A minimal recovery and deployment environment
A full desktop edition of Windows
A Linux-based disk imaging utility
A permanent replacement operating system
explain: WinPE is a lightweight Windows environment used for recovery, installation, and deployment tasks, not a full desktop OS.

q: Why is sideloading apps on a phone considered a security risk?
options: It disables the phone's screen lock automatically
It requires the device to be rooted first
It encrypts apps so they cannot be scanned
It bypasses official store review and can install malware
explain: Sideloaded apps bypass the checks in official app stores, so a malicious app can be installed without vetting.

q: What does the netstat -ano command display on a Windows PC?
options: The DNS resolver cache and its entries
Active connections along with their process IDs
The routing table and default gateway
The IP address configuration of each adapter
explain: The -ano flags list all connections and listening ports numerically, with the owning process ID for each.

q: What is the main purpose of Secure Boot during system startup?
options: To block unsigned or untrusted bootloaders
To speed up the boot process significantly
To scan installed applications for malware
To encrypt the drive before Windows loads
explain: Secure Boot checks bootloader signatures against trusted keys, which stops rootkits and unsigned boot code from loading.

q: What does formatting a partition do?
options: It prepares the partition with a filesystem
It divides one physical disk into volumes
It encrypts the existing data in place
It repairs errors in the current filesystem
explain: Formatting creates a filesystem structure on a partition so the OS can store files, and it removes existing data in the process.

q: What changes when a user enables Developer Mode on a Chromebook?
options: It enables deeper system access with security trade-offs
It switches the device to a Windows shell
It makes verified boot protection stronger
It locks the device to managed apps only
explain: Developer Mode turns off verified boot and grants shell-level access, which is useful for development but weakens built-in protections.

q: What happens during a clean install of Windows?
options: Files and apps are kept while Windows refreshes
The drive is wiped and Windows is reinstalled fresh
Only corrupted system files are replaced in place
User profiles migrate to a new domain automatically
explain: A clean install erases the target partition and installs Windows from scratch, so data and apps must be backed up and restored separately.

q: How should a technician describe Last Known Good Configuration on a modern Windows system?
options: As the primary rollback tool in Windows 11
As a current feature that replaces restore points
As a backup of the user's personal files
As a legacy rollback option superseded by newer recovery tools
explain: Last Known Good Configuration was a legacy boot option; modern Windows relies on System Restore, WinRE, and reset options instead.

q: A roaming profile fails to load at sign-in. What should a technician check first?
options: Server free space and network connectivity to the profile share
The local monitor's display and brightness settings
The user's local printer and default paper size
The workstation's sound and microphone input levels
explain: Roaming profiles are stored on a server, so share availability, free space, permissions, and the network path are the first checks.

q: What is the dig command used for on macOS and Linux systems?
options: Testing basic connectivity to a remote host
Querying DNS servers for detailed record information
Displaying the local IP address configuration
Tracing the route packets take to a destination
explain: Dig performs detailed DNS lookups and shows the question, answer, authority, and timing sections of the response.

q: In Device Manager, what does a yellow exclamation mark (yellow bang) next to a device indicate?
options: The device has been disabled by an administrator
The device is hidden and no longer present
The device is working and using a signed driver
The device has a problem, usually a driver issue
explain: A yellow bang marks a problem state, most often a missing, corrupt, or incompatible driver; the device status in Properties gives the error code.

q: How can Windows Firewall be configured to control individual programs?
options: It can only allow or block all traffic at once
It applies one hardware rule to every program
It requires all rules to be set on the router
It can block or allow traffic per application
explain: Windows Defender Firewall supports inbound and outbound rules scoped to a specific program, port, or protocol.

q: How should a backup schedule be chosen for a small business?
options: Always run a full backup every hour of the day
It should balance the recovery point objective against available resources
Back up only servers and ignore workstations
Copy files manually whenever a user remembers to
explain: The schedule should match how much data loss the business can tolerate (its RPO) while staying realistic for storage, bandwidth, and time.

q: What does the DISM tool repair in Windows?
options: The boot configuration data store only
User file permissions on NTFS volumes
Errors on the physical disk surface only
Corruption in the Windows component store image
explain: DISM services the Windows image and repairs component store corruption, which also lets SFC restore protected system files correctly.

q: A headset microphone produces no input in an app. What should be checked first?
options: That the correct input device and levels are selected, with mic access allowed
That the speakers are set as the default output device for all applications
That the display refresh rate matches the conferencing app's video settings
That the keyboard layout and regional format are correct for the user account
explain: The app and Windows privacy settings must allow microphone access, and the headset must be selected as the input device with usable levels.

q: When is exFAT the best filesystem choice?
options: For the Windows system drive on an internal desktop or laptop disk
For very small USB drives that only hold documents under 32 MB
As a replacement for NTFS permissions and encryption on a server
For large files on removable media shared between Windows and macOS
explain: exFAT supports files larger than 4 GB and works natively on Windows and macOS, making it ideal for large external drives and flash media.

q: What is the central challenge a BYOD policy must balance?
options: Banning personal devices from the building entirely
Balancing user privacy with corporate control of company data
Providing free phones to every employee
Ignoring security so employees stay productive
explain: BYOD policies protect company data, often through containerization or work profiles, while respecting the employee's personal data and privacy.

q: When should a technician use driver rollback in Device Manager?
options: To install the newest driver from the vendor
To update the operating system to a new build
To revert to the previous driver after a bad update
To remove the device and its software permanently
explain: Roll Back Driver restores the previously installed driver package, which is the quick fix when a new driver breaks a working device.

q: Which statement about biometric authentication is most accurate?
options: It can never fail to recognize a legitimate user, even in poor lighting
It is convenient but has physical and legal limits, so a fallback is needed
It completely replaces the need for any password, PIN, or fallback method
It cannot be spoofed under any circumstances, even with a detailed replica
explain: Biometrics are convenient, but a compromised fingerprint or face cannot be changed like a password, and recognition can fail, so a strong fallback remains necessary.

q: A technician finds an unfamiliar process using heavy CPU. What is the best first step?
options: End the process immediately without checking it
Rename the executable so it cannot restart
Disable all startup programs on the machine
Research the process from trusted sources before ending it
explain: Some unfamiliar processes are legitimate system or app components; verifying the name, publisher, and file path first avoids breaking Windows or an application.

q: Which list orders common screen-lock methods from weakest to strongest protection?
options: PIN, then password, then pattern, then swipe, then biometrics alone
Password, then biometrics alone, then PIN, then swipe, then pattern
Pattern, then swipe, then password, then PIN, then fingerprint only
Swipe, then pattern, then PIN, then password, then biometrics with MFA
explain: A simple swipe offers almost no protection, patterns and short PINs are stronger, long passwords are stronger still, and biometrics combined with MFA provide the strongest listed option.

q: Why is clear communication with a customer important during a repair?
options: It sets realistic expectations about findings, cost, and timing
It allows the technician to skip testing the fix
It replaces the need to document the repair
It guarantees the customer will approve extra work
explain: Explaining findings in plain language and setting expectations about time, cost, and outcome prevents misunderstandings and builds trust.

q: Why should jailbroken or rooted phones be blocked from corporate resources?
options: They receive operating system updates too quickly
They use more battery than managed devices
They break the OS security model and bypass sandboxing
They cannot connect to corporate Wi-Fi networks
explain: Jailbreaking and rooting remove sandbox and signature protections, so malware and data leakage become much harder to control; MDM should detect and quarantine such devices.

q: What useful information does a Windows blue screen (BSOD) provide?
options: A stop code that is logged for troubleshooting
A guarantee that the computer must be replaced
Proof that the failure was caused by malware
A backup copy of the user's open documents
explain: The stop code and the resulting dump and event logs point to faulty drivers, hardware, or system files, which guides the diagnosis.

q: What is the role of an intrusion detection system (IDS) on a network?
options: To block malicious traffic inline automatically
To assign IP addresses to network devices
To encrypt traffic between network segments
To detect and alert on intrusions without blocking traffic itself
explain: An IDS passively monitors and alerts on suspicious activity; an IPS sits inline and can actively block the traffic.

q: What makes a strong WPA2 Wi-Fi passphrase?
options: Using the network name as the passphrase
Using a long, unique passphrase not used elsewhere
Using the default passphrase printed by a neighbor
Using a short word that is easy to share
explain: Long, unique passphrases resist dictionary and brute-force attacks against the WPA2 handshake far better than short or reused ones.

q: What does a system image backup capture?
options: Only the user's documents, pictures, and music folders on the drive
Only the operating system registry settings and installed updates
The entire OS, applications, settings, and files for a full restore
A list of installed programs so they can be downloaded again later
explain: A system image is a complete snapshot of the system volume that can restore the whole machine to that state in one operation.

q: A user's microphone works in one app but not in another. What is the most likely cause to check?
options: A failed motherboard audio chipset
A disconnected internal speaker cable
The app's privacy permission and selected input device
A corrupted Windows boot configuration store
explain: Per-app microphone permissions and the input selected inside the app commonly block sound while other apps continue to work.

q: What does a smart card provide for user authentication?
options: A software token stored in the browser cache
Hardware-backed authentication using a certificate on the card
A printed backup code for password resets
A contactless payment method for office purchases
explain: Smart cards such as CAC and PIV cards hold certificates and private keys in hardware, providing strong two-factor authentication with a PIN.

q: Group Policy settings are not applying to a workstation. What should a technician do first?
options: Reinstall Windows on the affected workstation
Delete the user's profile and start over
Disable the local firewall and antivirus
Run gpupdate and check policy processing and replication
explain: Forcing a policy refresh with gpupdate and reviewing results with gpresult shows whether policies are reaching the machine and which ones applied or failed.

q: A scheduled backup job keeps failing. What should a technician check first?
options: The workstation's wallpaper and theme settings
The user's email client signature settings
Available disk space, VSS writer status, and the backup logs
The monitor cable and display resolution settings
explain: Full destination storage, failed Volume Shadow Copy writers, and errors recorded in the backup logs account for most backup failures.

q: Why should a smartphone's storage be encrypted?
options: So the phone can connect to any Wi-Fi network
So apps load faster after a system update
So the carrier can locate the phone more easily
So data stays protected if the device is lost or stolen
explain: Encryption makes stored data unreadable without the passcode, which protects personal and company information on a lost or stolen phone.

q: Where are Offline Files sync conflicts reviewed and resolved in Windows?
options: In Disk Management under the volume properties
In Event Viewer under the Application log
In Sync Center, where conflicting versions can be compared
In Device Manager under the network adapter
explain: Sync Center shows Offline Files conflicts and lets the user keep the local version, the server version, or both after reconnecting.

q: Device Manager lists a device as an Unknown device. What is the correct next step?
options: Remove the device entry and ignore the hardware
Format the drive and reinstall Windows
Identify the device and install its correct driver
Disable the device so the warning disappears
explain: An unknown device is hardware without a working driver; its hardware IDs identify it so the correct vendor driver can be installed.

q: Why should backup restores be tested regularly?
options: To satisfy the antivirus software requirements
To delete older backups and save storage space
To prove the backups can actually restore data when needed
To update the backup software to a new version
explain: Untested backups often fail because of corrupt media, missing pieces, or wrong settings; a test restore verifies the whole process before an emergency.

q: An employee finds an unlabeled USB flash drive in the parking lot. What should they do?
options: Never plug it in and hand it to IT security
Plug it in to identify who owns it
Format it and use it as a spare drive
Plug it in and scan it with antivirus first
explain: Unknown USB devices are a known malware delivery method, so the drive should never be connected and should be turned over to IT.

q: A user receives an MFA push prompt they did not request. What should they do?
options: Deny it and secure the account immediately
Ignore it and continue working as normal
Share the prompt code with a coworker
Approve it so the prompts stop appearing
explain: An unsolicited MFA prompt usually means someone has the password and is trying to sign in, so it should be denied and the account password changed and reviewed.

q: A user's mapped network drive is missing after sign-in. What should a technician check first?
options: Whether the local printer has enough paper
Check the Group Policy or logon script and network connectivity to the share
Whether the user's monitor is set to extend
Whether the workstation clock shows the right time zone only
explain: Persistent mappings are usually applied by Group Policy or a logon script, and they fail when the policy, script, or network path to the share is broken.

q: A PC is very slow and a malware infection is suspected. How should it be scanned?
options: Run a quick scan while all apps stay open
Scan in Safe Mode or with an offline scanner
Defragment the drive before scanning anything
Replace the computer without scanning it first
explain: Safe Mode and offline scans load fewer drivers and services, which helps expose rootkits and malware that hide during a normal boot.

q: A user cannot send or receive email in a desktop client. What should be checked first?
options: The account settings, server ports, and authentication credentials
The size of the user's mailbox archive and its oldest saved messages
The mail client's theme, reading pane layout, and default font sizes
The workstation's screensaver timeout and current power plan settings
explain: Wrong server names, ports, encryption settings, or credentials are the most common causes of a client that suddenly stops sending and receiving.

q: A user reports a tingling feeling from a PC's metal case. What is the correct response?
options: Advise the user to open the case and fix the wiring fault themselves
Treat it as a minor cosmetic issue and keep using the PC as normal
Replace the power supply unit and continue testing the PC at the desk
Treat it as a ground fault and refer it to a qualified electrician
explain: A tingling case suggests a grounding problem that can be a shock hazard; electrical faults are handled by a qualified electrician, not end users or PC technicians.

q: What does System Restore roll back on a Windows PC?
options: All of the user's personal documents and photos
The entire drive to its factory state
System files, drivers, and settings to a restore point
Only the web browser's history and cache
explain: System Restore returns system files, registry settings, drivers, and installed programs to a restore point without removing personal files.

q: A Windows PC hangs whenever the user tries to shut it down. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the monitor supports the current resolution
Whether the keyboard layout matches the region
Processes or services that are hanging and blocking shutdown
Whether the desktop has too many shortcut icons
explain: A process or service that will not close can stall shutdown; Event Viewer and Task Manager help identify the blocker.

q: How is a corrupted Windows bootloader most commonly repaired?
options: By replacing the computer's power supply with a known-good spare unit
By booting recovery media and repairing the boot configuration
By reinstalling every application and driver currently stored on the PC
By clearing the web browser's cache, cookies, and saved site history
explain: Booting from Windows recovery media gives access to Startup Repair and tools such as bootrec that rebuild the BCD and boot records.

q: A PC displays a locked screen demanding payment to unlock files (ransomware). What should be done?
options: Pay the ransom quickly to restore the files
Isolate the PC and restore from a clean backup
Keep the PC online so files can be recovered
Ignore the message and continue working normally
explain: The infected machine should be disconnected to stop spread and encryption, cleaned or rebuilt, and restored from a known-good backup rather than paying the ransom.

q: A domain user account is locked out. Where can an administrator unlock it?
options: In the local printer's management console
By deleting the account and recreating it
In Active Directory Users and Computers or the local users tool
By restarting the user's workstation three times
explain: Account lockout is cleared in the account management tool (ADUC for domain accounts), where the administrator can also review failed sign-in attempts and lockout policy.

q: How do cloud disaster recovery tiers such as pilot light and warm standby differ?
options: They differ only in the color of the console
They balance recovery cost against recovery time objectives
They are two names for the same backup job
They differ only in which users can access them
explain: Higher DR tiers keep more resources running in the cloud, costing more but restoring service faster; the choice is driven by the recovery time objective.

q: A popup claims the PC is infected and tells the user to call a phone number for help. What is this?
options: A legitimate Windows security notification
A genuine antivirus renewal reminder
A scheduled Windows update warning
A fake antivirus scam that should not be clicked or called
explain: Real antivirus products do not demand a phone call or payment through a browser popup; the popup should be closed, ideally via Task Manager, and the PC scanned.

q: What is BitLocker used for in Windows?
options: Scanning drives for viruses and spyware
Encrypting Windows drives to protect data at rest
Compressing drives to save storage space
Backing up drives to cloud storage automatically
explain: BitLocker is full-drive encryption that protects data if a drive or laptop is lost or stolen; its recovery key should be backed up separately.

q: Why should a technician label parts and screws during disassembly?
options: To make the workbench look more professional for visiting customers
To slow the repair process down so additional billable time accrues
To impress the customer with how organized the repair process looks
To make reassembly faster and prevent leftover or misplaced parts
explain: Labels, photos, and organized trays keep screws and parts matched to their locations, which prevents mistakes and leftover hardware during reassembly.

q: Where do Chromebooks primarily store user data by default?
options: In the cloud, using Google Drive
Only on the internal local drive
Only on a removable USB drive
On a local Windows file server
explain: ChromeOS is cloud-first, so files are stored in Google Drive by default, with offline access enabled for selected files.

q: A rootkit is suspected on a Windows PC. What is the safest response?
options: Run a quick scan and return the PC to service
Remove it with a standard in-Windows cleanup
Run an offline scan or rebuild the system from clean media
Delete the browser history and temporary files
explain: Rootkits hide deep in the system and are hard to verify as fully removed, so an offline scan or a clean rebuild is the safest course.

q: What does a zero trust security model require?
options: Trusting all devices on the local network
Verifying every access request, regardless of location
Buying one specific vendor's security product
Removing passwords from all user accounts
explain: Zero trust assumes a breach is possible and continuously authenticates and authorizes every user, device, and access request.

q: A user's fingerprint sign-in has stopped working reliably. What should be tried first?
options: Replace the fingerprint reader hardware
Disable biometric sign-in permanently
Re-enroll the user's fingerprint
Reinstall Windows on the device
explain: Re-enrolling refreshes the stored biometric template, which commonly fixes gradual recognition failures before any hardware is replaced.

q: An employee leaves the company and their personal phone was enrolled in BYOD. What should the remote wipe target?
options: The employee's entire phone, including personal photos
Only the corporate data and work profile on the device
The employee's personal cloud account as well
Nothing, because BYOD devices cannot be wiped
explain: A selective wipe removes company apps and data from the work container while leaving the employee's personal data untouched.

q: How should location services be configured on a work phone?
options: Enabled for every app at all times
Disabled even for navigation and safety apps
Limited to the apps that genuinely need location access
Hidden so the user cannot change any setting
explain: Granting location only to apps that need it, preferably while the app is in use, reduces tracking and data exposure.

q: What does a legal hold require an organization to do?
options: Delete data that might be used in court
Stop all backups until the case is finished
Copy all company data to a personal drive
Preserve relevant data and suspend its normal deletion
explain: A legal hold preserves electronically stored information related to litigation, overriding normal retention and deletion schedules.

q: How should mobile and desktop app permissions be managed?
options: Grant every permission an app requests
Review them and grant only the minimum each app needs
Ignore them once the app is installed
Grant location and microphone access to all apps
explain: Reviewing permissions and minimizing them — for example denying location or microphone access an app does not need — follows least-privilege practice.

q: After an incident is resolved, what prevents the same incident from recurring?
options: Installing antivirus on one workstation
Closing the ticket as quickly as possible
Identifying and closing the root cause of the incident
Deleting the incident report and its logs
explain: Post-incident work should find and fix the underlying cause, with corrective actions tracked to completion so the problem does not return.

q: Why should a restore point be created before making major system changes?
options: It creates a full backup of all user files
It replaces the need for any other backup
It speeds up the installation of new drivers
It enables rollback if the change causes problems
explain: A restore point captures system files and settings before a driver or software change, so the system can be rolled back if the change breaks something.

q: Which backup combination is the most space-efficient for daily backups?
options: A full backup copied to three separate drives
A differential backup with no full backup
A full backup followed by incremental backups
Identical full backups taken every hour
explain: Incremental backups store only changes since the last backup, so a full backup plus incrementals uses the least space, though restores need the full chain.

q: Which filesystem is the standard for Windows system drives?
options: exFAT, designed mainly for removable media
FAT32, with a 4 GB maximum file size
NTFS, with permissions, encryption, and large-file support
APFS, designed for Apple devices only
explain: NTFS is Windows' standard filesystem and supports file permissions, encryption, journaling, and very large files and volumes.

q: What is the purpose of an RMA process?
options: To register software licenses with a vendor
To schedule on-site service for any device
To request a refund for a software subscription
To return faulty hardware to the vendor for repair or replacement
explain: An RMA authorizes the return of defective hardware; documenting the fault clearly helps the vendor process the repair or replacement smoothly.

q: A hard drive has physically failed and the data was not backed up. What is the realistic recovery option?
options: Run a free recovery app on the failed drive
Open the drive and repair it at the desk
Freeze the drive and then copy its files
Send it to a specialist data recovery service with a clean room
explain: Recovering data from a mechanically dead drive is specialist clean-room work that is expensive, which is why tested backups matter.

q: What do File History (Windows) and Time Machine (macOS) have in common?
options: They keep versioned backups of user files
They require a server to store any backup
They create bootable images of the whole system
They back up only cloud-synced documents
explain: Both tools keep historical versions of user files, so an overwritten or deleted file can be restored from an earlier version.

q: What should an organization do immediately after confirming a security breach?
options: Follow the incident response plan to contain and investigate
Delete affected systems to remove the evidence
Hide the breach from management and regulators
Wait to see whether the problem happens again
explain: The incident response plan drives containment, eradication, recovery, communication, and later lessons learned in a controlled order.

q: Why should network switch configurations be backed up regularly?
options: To document which cables are plugged in
To record user passwords for the network team
To update the switch firmware automatically
To enable fast recovery by restoring the configuration after failure or replacement
explain: A saved configuration lets a replacement or reset switch be restored to service quickly without rebuilding VLANs and settings by hand.

q: What is Device Manager used for in Windows?
options: Managing hardware devices and their drivers
Changing the desktop wallpaper and themes
Installing and removing Windows applications
Editing documents stored on the computer
explain: Device Manager shows installed hardware, driver status and versions, and problem devices marked with warning icons.

q: How does network segmentation improve security?
options: It limits the blast radius by containing breaches to one segment
It removes the need for any firewall rules
It speeds up traffic between all departments
It allows every device to reach every server
explain: VLANs and firewalls between segments contain lateral movement, so a compromise in one area does not automatically expose the rest of the network.

q: What does a smart card reader read?
options: The SIM card inside a mobile phone
The magnetic stripe on a payment card
The barcode printed on an asset tag
CAC or PIV cards used for strong authentication
explain: Smart card readers read CAC and PIV credential cards that store certificates for government and enterprise authentication.

q: What is a live Linux USB most useful for?
options: Replacing Windows as the permanent desktop
Troubleshooting and recovering data without installing an OS
Installing Linux automatically on every boot
Formatting drives so data cannot be recovered
explain: A live environment boots from USB without changing the installed system, which is useful for testing hardware and copying data from a Windows install that will not boot.

q: A laptop repeatedly prompts for the BitLocker recovery key at every boot. What should be checked first?
options: Whether TPM and boot configuration changes are triggering recovery
The laptop's screen brightness settings
Whether the user has too many desktop files
Whether the Wi-Fi network name has changed
explain: Repeated recovery prompts usually follow TPM, Secure Boot, firmware, or hardware changes; the boot configuration should be checked and protection suspended during hardware work.

q: What does BitLocker on a laptop require to protect its drive?
options: Only an administrator account on the laptop
Only a Windows password at sign-in
Nothing beyond a standard Windows install
A TPM or startup key, with the recovery key saved safely
explain: BitLocker uses a TPM or a startup key to unlock the drive, and the recovery key must be backed up or a board failure can permanently lock the data.

q: What does 802.1X do on a wired or wireless network?
options: It authenticates a device or user before granting network access
It provides guest access without any sign-in
It encrypts all traffic between two switches
It assigns IP addresses to connecting devices
explain: 802.1X is port-based network access control that authenticates the supplicant through a server such as RADIUS before the port allows normal traffic.

q: A workstation is actively encrypting files as part of a ransomware infection. What is the first action?
options: Pay the ransom before more files are lost
Isolate the workstation immediately and restore from backup after cleanup
Ignore it until the weekly scan runs
Email the files to another workstation for safety
explain: Isolating the machine stops the encryption and lateral spread; recovery then comes from clean backups, not from paying the ransom first.

q: A shipment arrives with visible damage to the box and device. What should be done first?
options: Discard the packaging and test the device
Document the damage immediately with photos for a claim
Install the device and report damage later
Return the device without recording its condition
explain: Photographing and documenting shipping damage as soon as it is received supports the carrier or vendor claim and protects the organization.

q: What is required before a user can safely use mobile payments on a phone?
options: A device screen lock and verified payment cards
No screen lock, so payments complete faster
A store account with no payment card added
A rooted phone with a custom operating system
explain: Mobile payment systems rely on tokenization and require device authentication, such as a screen lock and biometrics, plus verified cards before use.

q: A PC reports a TPM error after a firmware update. What may be needed?
options: Replacing the motherboard in every case
A TPM firmware update or clearing the TPM, with recovery keys backed up first
Disabling BitLocker permanently for safety
Reinstalling all applications on the PC
explain: TPM errors after firmware changes are often resolved by a TPM firmware update or a clear, but clearing can affect BitLocker, so recovery keys must be saved first.

q: How do work profiles separate data on a mobile device?
options: They copy personal apps into a shared folder
They merge work and personal data for backup
They delete personal data when work apps install
They isolate business apps and data from personal apps and data
explain: A work profile keeps corporate apps and data in a separate container, which allows selective wipe of work data without touching personal content.

q: Why is proper lifting technique important when handling servers and heavy equipment?
options: It protects the technician's back from injury
It makes the equipment easier to install quickly
It is only required for professional movers
It prevents static discharge to the equipment
explain: Servers and UPS units are heavy; lifting with the legs, keeping the load close, and getting help prevents back injuries.

q: Users report very slow domain logons. What should a technician investigate?
options: The color depth set on each user's monitor
The number of icons on each user's desktop
Group Policy processing, logon scripts, and network connectivity
The default font used in the email client
explain: Oversized roaming profiles, slow or failing Group Policy processing, logon scripts, and network problems are the usual causes of slow logons.

q: On what basis does a firewall decide to block or allow traffic?
options: The color coding of the network cables plugged into each switch port
The maximum link speed of the connecting device and its network cable
Ports, IP addresses, and increasingly the application or user
The date the connecting device was purchased and first put into service
explain: Firewall rules match traffic by addresses, ports, and protocols, and modern firewalls can also filter by application and user identity.

q: A laptop's built-in webcam does not work in any app. What should be checked first?
options: The privacy shutter, app permissions, and camera driver
Reinstall the operating system completely
Replace the laptop with a newer model
The laptop's battery health and charge cycles
explain: A closed physical shutter, a disabled camera in privacy settings, or a bad driver accounts for most built-in webcam failures.

q: HDR video looks washed out on a Windows display. What should be adjusted first?
options: Replace the monitor with an SDR model
Increase the desktop scaling to 200 percent
Calibrate the SDR and HDR brightness balance for the display
Disable HDR permanently on all displays
explain: Windows HDR often needs per-display tuning of the SDR content brightness slider and HDR calibration before the picture looks correct.

q: Why is documenting an incident as it happens important?
options: It allows tickets to be closed without resolution
It replaces the need for an incident response plan
It creates an accurate timeline of events and actions taken
It hides mistakes made during the response
explain: Contemporaneous notes create a reliable timeline that supports investigation, reporting, handovers, and later review.

q: What is the role of a TPM chip in a Windows PC?
options: It stores the user's documents securely
It secures cryptographic keys and supports features such as BitLocker
It acts as a software password manager
It manages the passwords typed into websites
explain: A Trusted Platform Module is a hardware chip that stores keys and measurements used by BitLocker, Secure Boot attestation, and credential protection.

q: A Windows update causes the PC to loop back into recovery at every boot. What is the best recovery step?
options: Replace the PC because updates cannot be undone
Leave the PC looping until the next update
Boot into recovery and uninstall the problematic update
Delete the user's profile and all documents
explain: WinRE and Safe Mode let the technician uninstall the latest quality or feature update that is preventing a normal boot.

q: Which statement about biometric sign-in, such as Windows Hello, is correct?
options: It is inherently insecure and should be disabled
It adds convenience and keeps a PIN or password as a fallback
It fully replaces passwords on every system
It works even when the sensor is damaged
explain: Biometrics speed up sign-in, but a fallback PIN or password is still required because sensors fail and biometrics can be unavailable or compelled.

q: An email attachment arrives unexpectedly from a known contact with an urgent request to open it. What should the user do?
options: Never open it until it has been verified as expected and safe
Open it quickly before antivirus can block it
Forward it to coworkers so they can check it
Save it to a shared drive for the team
explain: Unexpected attachments are a primary malware and phishing vector; they should not be opened and should be verified with the sender through a separate channel.

q: A company issues a tablet for field work. What must be configured before it is used?
options: Only a protective case and screen film
A selection of games for downtime use
Nothing, because tablets need no management
MDM enrollment and device encryption
explain: Enrolling the tablet in mobile device management and enabling encryption lets IT enforce policy, deploy apps, and remotely wipe a lost device.

q: A user gets 'Access Denied' when opening a shared printer. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the printer is out of toner today
The share permissions and NTFS permissions on the printer
Whether the user's keyboard is working correctly
Whether the print server needs a new monitor
explain: Both share permissions and security (NTFS-style) permissions must allow the user; a denial usually means one of them is missing or set to deny.

q: A user plugs in a USB headset but sound still plays through the laptop speakers. What should be checked?
options: Whether the laptop display is set to duplicate
Whether the headset is set as the correct default playback device
Whether the keyboard backlight is turned on
Whether the Wi-Fi adapter is using 5 GHz
explain: Windows keeps separate playback devices; selecting the headset as the default output (and input, if needed) in Sound settings routes audio correctly.

q: A backup fails with a VSS error. What is a common fix?
options: Check the VSS writers and restart the failed writer service
Reinstall Windows to repair the snapshot service
Ignore the error because backups still complete
Format the backup destination drive immediately
explain: VSS writers that are in a failed state block snapshot-based backups; listing the writers and restarting the affected service or provider often clears the error.

q: Why should smartphone OS updates be installed promptly?
options: They patch security flaws that attackers actively exploit
They mainly change the phone's appearance
They are required to keep the phone's warranty
They are needed for the phone to make calls
explain: Mobile OS updates fix known vulnerabilities; delaying them leaves the device exposed to exploits that are already public.

q: Which statement correctly describes the FAT32 filesystem?
options: It is used only on internal Windows drives
It is broadly compatible but limits a single file to 4 GB
It is the newest filesystem for Windows servers
It has no file-size or partition limits at all
explain: FAT32 works across almost all operating systems and devices, but its 4 GB per-file limit makes exFAT or NTFS better for large files.

q: What does the Windows Offline Files feature do?
options: Deletes network files automatically when the user logs off the computer
Requires the user to remain connected to the office network at all times
Caches network files locally and syncs changes when reconnected
Copies every local file to every other workstation on the office network
explain: Offline Files (client-side caching) keeps a local copy of network files so work continues without connectivity, then syncs changes on reconnect.

q: What makes a forensic disk image suitable for use as evidence?
options: It is a bit-for-bit copy verified with cryptographic hashes
It is a standard file copy made in Explorer
It is compressed so it loads faster in court
It is edited to remove irrelevant files first
explain: A forensic image duplicates every bit of the source and is verified against hashes, proving the copy matches the original exactly.

q: What does an in-place upgrade (repair install) of Windows do?
options: It performs a clean install and deletes all files
It removes all applications and user settings
It refreshes Windows while keeping files, apps, and settings
It converts the installation to a Linux system
explain: An in-place upgrade reinstalls Windows over itself, repairing OS problems while preserving user files, applications, and most settings.

q: How do retail parts generally differ from OEM parts?
options: OEM parts always carry the longest warranty
The two types are identical in every respect
OEM parts are sold only in retail stores
Retail parts typically include better warranty and vendor support
explain: Retail-boxed parts usually include the manufacturer's full warranty and support, while OEM parts often carry shorter coverage handled through the system builder.

q: An update to a graphics driver breaks the display. What should the technician do?
options: Keep the broken driver and lower the brightness
Replace the graphics card with a new one
Roll back to the previous working driver
Reinstall Windows to restore the display
explain: Rolling back in Device Manager restores the previous driver package, which is the standard recovery after a bad driver update.

q: What is macOS Migration Assistant used to do?
options: Migrate virtual machines between two host servers
Move a Boot Camp partition to another drive
Transfer accounts, files, apps, and settings to a new Mac
Transfer an iPhone backup to an Android phone
explain: Migration Assistant moves user accounts, files, applications, and settings from an old Mac, a Time Machine backup, or a Windows PC during setup or later from Utilities.

q: Malware identified as a keylogger is found on a user's PC. What must be done after removing it?
options: Remove it and change the user's passwords, assuming credentials were captured
Keep the same passwords because the infection is gone
Treat stored browser cookies as the only risk
Return the PC with no further action needed
explain: A keylogger records keystrokes, so removal alone is not enough; passwords used on the machine should be changed and accounts reviewed.

q: What is the purpose of an anti-static mat on a repair bench?
options: To ground the work surface and drain static safely
To serve as a cushioned mouse pad for comfort
To insulate components from the bench ground
To magnetically hold screws during a repair
explain: An anti-static mat, used with a wrist strap, provides a grounded, static-dissipative surface that protects components from ESD.

q: What does the CHKDSK utility check and repair in Windows?
options: Fragmentation levels across the hard drive
Disk and filesystem integrity, with /f to fix errors
Faulty sectors inside system memory modules
Errors in the Windows registry hives only
explain: CHKDSK examines the filesystem and disk surface for errors and, with switches such as /f and /r, repairs logical errors and marks bad sectors.

q: After malware is cleaned from a network, what best prevents reinfection?
options: Relying on antivirus software alone as the organization's only defense
Accepting that reinfection cannot be prevented and taking no further action
Patching systems, keeping AV updated, maintaining backups, and training users
Removing all backups and restore points so malware has nowhere to hide
explain: Layered prevention — patching, updated anti-malware, tested backups, least privilege, and user training — addresses the ways malware returns.

q: What is the correct sequence of response when a PC is found to be infected with malware?
options: Keep using it normally until the next scheduled weekly antivirus scan runs
Reinstall Windows immediately as the first step in every infection case
Isolate it, scan and remove the malware, then verify it is clean
Delete the user's documents and pictures, and then close the support ticket
explain: Isolating the machine stops spread, after which scanning, removal, and verification confirm the infection is gone before it returns to service.

q: A company changes its shared Wi-Fi password (PSK). What must happen next?
options: The new password must be entered on every device that uses that network
Only the administrator's laptop needs updating
Nothing, because devices update automatically
The router must be replaced with a new model
explain: A changed shared passphrase must be updated on every client device; enterprise 802.1X authentication avoids this shared-secret problem.

q: Which precautions protect components from electrostatic discharge during repair?
options: Working on carpet while wearing a wool sweater
Handling boards only by their connector pins
Keeping components inside a sealed plastic bag
Using a wrist strap and anti-static mat to stay grounded
explain: Grounding the technician with a wrist strap and mat equalizes potential and drains static before it can damage sensitive chips.

q: An employee must use open hotel Wi-Fi for work. How can the connection be made safer?
options: Use a VPN because open networks expose traffic to sniffing
It is safe as soon as any web page loads
It encrypts itself once a password is entered
It needs no caution because hotel networks are trusted
explain: Open Wi-Fi traffic can be intercepted by others on the network; a VPN encrypts the traffic through that untrusted connection.

q: What does a product warranty protect the buyer against?
options: Accidental damage from drops and liquid spills
Defects in materials or workmanship during the coverage period
Normal wear and tear after many years of use
Damage caused by unauthorized modifications
explain: A warranty covers manufacturing defects for a set period; registering the product and keeping receipts makes a claim easier.

q: How can Point and Print restrictions affect printer deployment in a domain?
options: They change the default paper size for users
They may block users from installing shared printer drivers
They assign printers based on the user's location
They encrypt print jobs sent to the server
explain: Point and Print policies control whether users can install drivers from print servers, and restrictive settings can block driver installation, especially for non-admins.

q: A company laptop is stolen from an employee's car. What should happen immediately?
options: Wait about a week in case the laptop is found and returned on its own
Do nothing at all if the laptop happened to be powered off when stolen
Report it, remotely wipe it if possible, and change the user's passwords
Ask the employee to purchase a replacement laptop at their own expense
explain: Prompt reporting allows a remote wipe attempt, and changing passwords plus reviewing account activity limits what a thief can reach, especially with encryption in place.

q: A Windows update repeatedly fails to install. What should a technician check first?
options: The user's desktop wallpaper and icon layout
The age of the workstation's power cable
Available disk space, then run the Windows Update troubleshooter
The printer drivers installed on the machine
explain: Low disk space and stuck update components cause many failures; the troubleshooter and, if needed, resetting the update components address them.

q: Where should a smart TV be placed on a home or office network for best security?
options: On the main trusted LAN with all workstations
On a wired connection to the domain controller
On the IoT or guest network, isolated from trusted devices
It should never be connected to any network
explain: Smart TVs collect data and are rarely patched well, so isolating them on an IoT or guest segment protects the trusted network.

q: Several accounts lock out at once as one common password is tried against many users. What attack does this suggest, and what should happen?
options: It triggers lockouts and should be investigated as a password spray attack
It is normal sign-in behavior on busy mornings and needs no further review
It shows the domain controllers have run out of available storage space
It means every affected user's password was already changed automatically
explain: Password spraying tries one common password across many accounts to avoid per-account lockouts; correlated lockouts should be investigated in the sign-in logs.

q: An employee's account is confirmed to be compromised. What should IT do first?
options: Lock the account and reset its passwords and sessions
Ask the employee to pick a simpler password
Monitor the account quietly for another week
Delete the employee's mailbox and start over
explain: Locking or disabling the account, forcing a password reset, revoking sessions, and enabling MFA stops the attacker from continuing to use it.

q: What does partitioning a drive accomplish?
options: It creates a filesystem so files can be stored
It always erases every file on the drive
It divides one physical drive into separate logical volumes
It encrypts each section of the drive separately
explain: Partitioning divides a disk into logical sections that can then be formatted and used as separate volumes, such as separating the OS from data.

q: A network adapter works poorly with the generic driver Windows installed. What is the best fix?
options: Install the current driver from the device vendor
Replace the network adapter hardware
Reinstall the entire operating system
Disable the adapter and use Wi-Fi instead
explain: Vendor drivers provide full features and fixes that generic in-box drivers may lack, particularly for network adapters.

q: What is the purpose of a chain of custody form in an investigation?
options: To track who handled evidence, when, and how it was stored
To record the final verdict of the court
To authorize destruction of the seized device
To list the software installed on a suspect PC
explain: Chain of custody documents every transfer and handling of evidence so its integrity can be demonstrated later, including in court.

q: What is the goal of a lessons-learned review after an incident?
options: To assign blame to the person on call
To delete logs that might criticize the team
To close the ticket without any follow-up
To document what happened and improve future response
explain: A blameless lessons-learned review captures what worked and what failed so processes and systems improve before the next incident.

q: Why is evidence preservation important at the start of a security incident?
options: So drives can be reimaged as quickly as possible
So the affected user can keep working normally
So investigators avoid destroying logs and other evidence
So police can be given the user's password
explain: Reimaging, rebooting, or continued use can overwrite logs and artifacts; preserving evidence first keeps the investigation and any legal process viable.

q: A user reports a login alert for a sign-in they do not recognize. What should happen?
options: Ignore the alert completely if the account password still works today
Wait until the next monthly security review meeting to mention the alert
Disable multi-factor authentication so the sign-in alerts stop appearing
Verify the activity and secure the account if it was not the user
explain: An unrecognized sign-in should be checked in the sign-in logs, and the account secured with a password reset and session revocation if the activity is not legitimate.

q: Why should router firmware be kept up to date?
options: Firmware updates mainly add new themes
Routers stop working if firmware is updated
Updates are released only for cosmetic changes
Updates patch known vulnerabilities in the gateway
explain: Routers and gateways are common attack targets, and firmware updates close published vulnerabilities and improve stability.

q: A phone's battery suddenly drains twice as fast starting yesterday. What is the most targeted first check?
options: The phone's original manufacturing date and the age of its battery pack
The battery usage statistics by app, to find an update or stuck background process
The carrier's cell tower coverage map for the area where the phone is used
The wallpaper selection, its brightness setting, and the home screen layout
explain: Per-app battery statistics identify the specific app or stuck process — often sync, location, or streaming after an update — so it can be stopped, updated, or removed and the drain re-measured.

q: What is the primary function of a firewall?
options: To act as a network switch for local traffic
To assign routes between remote networks
To provide wireless access to nearby devices
To filter traffic according to a security policy
explain: A firewall enforces policy between network zones by allowing or blocking traffic based on rules for addresses, ports, protocols, and applications.

q: An employee receives a convincing phishing email asking for their password. What should they do?
options: Open it and follow the instructions quickly
Delete it and report it through the phishing process
Reply to the sender asking if it is real
Forward it to their personal email account
explain: Phishing messages should not be interacted with; deleting and reporting them lets security warn others and investigate, and senders should be verified through a separate channel.

q: What does it mean when a Windows driver is digitally signed?
options: It was originally downloaded from a third-party Linux software repository
Its publisher and integrity have been verified by Microsoft signing
It will always run noticeably faster than any comparable unsigned driver
It is permanently exempt from all Windows update and compatibility checks
explain: Driver signing verifies the publisher's identity and that the package has not been altered, and 64-bit Windows requires signed kernel drivers by default.

q: Why must a technician control static discharge before handling a motherboard?
options: Static only builds up during winter months
A discharge is harmless to modern components
Static improves the connection of seated cards
A static discharge can kill components, so ESD gear should be used
explain: Even a discharge too small to feel can damage chips, so wrist straps, mats, and equipotential bonding are standard practice.

q: What happens when Windows boots into Safe Mode?
options: Windows loads normally with all third-party drivers
Windows repairs every software problem automatically
Windows loads with a minimal set of drivers and services
Windows restores the system to its factory state
explain: Safe Mode starts Windows with basic drivers and services, which isolates whether a driver or startup program is causing a problem.

q: Why is UPnP considered a security risk on a home or office router?
options: It slows the router down noticeably whenever new devices connect to it
It can automatically open inbound ports without administrator approval
It requires every inbound port to be opened manually by an administrator
It encrypts all traffic so thoroughly that it can no longer be inspected
explain: UPnP lets applications open ports on demand, which can expose services to the internet without the owner's knowledge; disabling it and forwarding ports manually is safer.

q: A PC boots to a BitLocker recovery prompt after a hardware change. What does the user need to proceed?
options: The BitLocker recovery key for that drive
Permission to bypass the recovery screen
A full reinstall of Windows from media
A new TPM chip installed on the board
explain: Hardware and boot changes can trigger BitLocker recovery, and only the correct recovery key unlocks the drive, which is why keys must be backed up.

q: A desktop PC wakes from sleep at random times during the night. What should be checked?
options: Whether the room lights are left on
Whether the mouse pad is the right size
Wake timers and devices allowed to wake the computer
Whether the desktop icons are arranged in rows
explain: Wake timers, scheduled tasks, and devices such as network adapters with wake permission commonly rouse a PC; powercfg can identify the last wake source.

q: A firewall rule change was made but traffic is still blocked. What should be checked in the rule set?
options: The color assigned to each firewall rule
The name of the administrator who edited it
Whether the firewall has enough disk space
Whether the rules are processed in the intended order
explain: Most firewalls apply the first matching rule, so a blocking rule placed above an allow rule will win; rule order must be reviewed.

q: Files across a share are being renamed and encrypted in bulk. What should this behavior trigger?
options: A routine defragmentation of the file server
Immediate isolation as a likely ransomware event in progress
A password change at the next monthly cycle
Nothing, because bulk renames are normal activity
explain: Mass renaming and encryption is characteristic ransomware behavior; rapid isolation, guided by EDR alerts, can halt the encryption mid-attack.

q: A user's browser homepage and search engine changed without their knowledge. What does this most likely indicate?
options: A normal feature of the latest browser update
A problem with the user's internet provider
A browser hijack that requires resetting the browser and checking extensions
Damage to the computer's display adapter
explain: Hijackers alter the homepage, search provider, extensions, and shortcuts; resetting the browser and removing suspicious extensions and shortcut changes clears it.

q: Malware has been removed from a PC. What should happen before it returns to service?
options: Verification with a second scanner or second opinion scan
A reinstall of every application on the PC
Nothing further, because removal is complete
Deletion of all restore points and backups
explain: A follow-up scan with a different tool confirms the system is clean and catches anything the first removal missed.

q: How does a remote wipe capability protect a lost phone?
options: It deletes the backups stored in the cloud
It locates the phone using the carrier bill
It locks the SIM card with the mobile carrier
It lets the owner erase the device through a service such as Find My
explain: Services such as Find My iPhone and Android's Find My Device can locate, lock, or erase a lost phone, but they must be enabled before the loss.

q: A user cannot sign in to their workstation. Which simple checks should come first?
options: Caps Lock, account lockout status, and whether the password is correct
Replace the workstation with a spare PC
Create a brand-new account for the user
Reinstall Windows to reset all credentials
explain: Most sign-in failures are simple: Caps Lock, a locked account after failed attempts, or an expired or mistyped password should be checked before deeper work.

q: Users cannot open a DFS namespace share. What should a technician check?
options: The file server's monitor and keyboard first
The sound settings on the user's workstation
DFS referrals and the health of the folder targets
The color of the network cable in the closet
explain: A namespace failure usually involves the namespace servers, referral ordering, or an unavailable folder target, all of which can be verified in DFS Management.

q: For what use case is tape backup still well suited?
options: As a fast replacement for a system disk
For sharing files between office workstations
For hourly backups of a live database
For long-term archival storage at low cost per terabyte
explain: LTO tape is inexpensive per terabyte and durable for cold, long-term archives, though restores are slower than disk-based backup.

q: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule require?
options: Three servers, two routers, and one switch
Three backups taken in one day each week
Three copies of data, on two different media, with one copy offsite
A RAID array with three mirrored disk pairs
explain: The rule keeps three copies of important data on two different types of media, with at least one copy stored offsite to survive a local disaster.

q: What is an 'evil twin' in wireless security?
options: A rogue access point that mimics a legitimate SSID to steal credentials
A backup access point used for failover
A second router that doubles network speed
A legitimate AP with a very strong signal
explain: An evil twin copies a trusted network name so users connect to the attacker, who can then capture credentials or traffic; certificate-based enterprise Wi-Fi helps prevent this.

q: What does running SFC /scannow do in Windows?
options: It checks the disk surface for bad sectors
It scans and repairs corrupted Windows system files
It removes all temporary files from the drive
It updates every installed device driver
explain: System File Checker compares protected system files against known-good copies and restores the corrupted ones, often after DISM repairs the component store.

q: When is physical destruction the appropriate data sanitization method?
options: For any paper documents leaving the office
For low-value drives that will be reused internally
When the highest assurance is needed and the media will not be reused
When a drive simply needs a quick format
explain: Shredding or otherwise destroying media guarantees the data cannot be recovered, making it the ultimate sanitization choice for highly sensitive data.

q: How should IoT devices such as cameras and smart plugs be connected to an office network?
options: Directly on the main LAN with all workstations
Trusted with full access to file servers
They should not be connected to any network
On a separate VLAN or network, isolated from trusted systems
explain: IoT devices are rarely patched and often insecure, so segmentation keeps a compromise from reaching workstations and servers.

q: Device Manager reports Code 43 for a USB device. What does this mean and what is the first step?
options: The device failed and Windows stopped it; reinstall its driver first
The device is working and needs no action
The computer must be replaced to clear the code
The error is caused by a full hard drive
explain: Code 43 means Windows stopped the device because it reported a failure; reinstalling or updating the driver is the first step, and persistent errors point to failing hardware.

q: What do AAA services such as RADIUS and TACACS+ provide?
options: Local accounts stored separately on each device
Wireless encryption for guest networks only
Centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting for network access
Automatic IP addressing for network devices
explain: AAA servers centralize who can sign in to network devices and services, what they may do, and an accounting record of their actions.

q: What is a honeynet in security research?
options: A network of honeypots that simulates a real network to study attackers
A production LAN segment for employee use
A backup network used during an outage
A marketing network that attracts new users
explain: A honeynet deploys multiple decoy systems that imitate a real network so attacker behavior can be observed safely without risking production assets.

q: An IPS sensor is deployed in promiscuous mode, receiving traffic from a SPAN port. What can it do?
options: It can block attacks inline like a firewall
It fails to see any traffic in this mode
It receives copied traffic, so it can only detect and alert like an IDS
It encrypts the traffic it monitors for safety
explain: A promiscuous sensor sees only a copy of the traffic and is not in the forwarding path, so it cannot block; blocking requires an inline deployment.

q: What is a magnetic parts tray used for during a repair?
options: It magnetizes components so they seat correctly
It stores screws and small parts in an organized way so they are not lost
It demagnetizes tools before they touch a drive
It tests whether a power supply is working
explain: A parts tray keeps screws grouped by step or location, preventing lost hardware during disassembly and reassembly.

q: A Windows PC is stuck in a loop, repeatedly trying to install the same update. What may be required?
options: Replacement of the PC with a newer model
Nothing, because update loops resolve permanently
A manual reset of the Windows Update components
Reinstallation of every application on the PC
explain: Stopping the update services and clearing the SoftwareDistribution download cache resets stuck update components so the update can download and install cleanly.

q: A user's browser opens unwanted search pages and toolbars keep reappearing. What is the best response?
options: Reset the browser and remove suspicious extensions
Reinstall Windows as the first step taken
Change the user's network password only
Ignore it because browser changes are harmless
explain: A browser hijack is cleared by resetting the browser, removing unknown extensions, and checking shortcuts and the default search engine, backed by a malware scan.

q: How do biometric devices such as fingerprint readers strengthen sign-in?
options: They eliminate the need for any other factor
They replace the operating system's lock screen
They make passwords easier to guess correctly
They add a hardware-based authentication factor to the sign-in process
explain: Fingerprint and face readers provide a convenient authentication factor, usually alongside a PIN or password fallback, as with Windows Hello.

q: Why is MAC address filtering considered weak wireless security?
options: Because MAC addresses can be observed and spoofed easily
Because it has never been bypassed in practice
Because it provides encryption equal to WPA3
Because it slows every wireless connection down
explain: Device MAC addresses are sent in the clear and are trivial to copy, so filtering adds little protection compared with WPA2 or WPA3 encryption.

q: How should a company control which mobile apps employees can install on work devices?
options: Allow any app the employee wants to install
Use an approved enterprise app catalog of vetted applications
Review apps only after an incident occurs
Install apps from links sent in text messages
explain: An enterprise app catalog or managed store limits installations to applications that have been reviewed for security and business need.

q: Several internal PCs are being redirected to fake websites even though DNS settings are correct. What should be inspected?
options: The PCs' desktop wallpaper settings
The PCs' battery and power settings
The printer queue on the file server
The hosts file, which malware may have edited to redirect sites
explain: Malware edits the local hosts file to redirect or block sites, including security vendor sites, so the file should be inspected and cleaned.

q: How should communication be handled while a major incident is in progress?
options: It should be improvised by whoever is available
It should be posted publicly as details emerge
It should be kept entirely secret from management
It should follow the incident response plan with designated communicators
explain: Following the plan, with a designated spokesperson and defined channels, keeps messages accurate and prevents leaks or conflicting statements.

q: A user reports no sound from a PC that worked yesterday. What should be checked first?
options: The default output device, volume, and mute state
Reinstall Windows to restore the audio stack
Replace the PC because the sound has failed
The network cable and its link speed
explain: Sound most often goes missing because the output was switched, muted, or turned down; checking the default device and volume precedes driver or hardware work.

q: Why might a technician disable Windows Fast Startup while troubleshooting?
options: Its hybrid shutdown can cause dual-boot and driver problems
It has no effect on the boot process at all
It always improves every dual-boot system
It is a feature found only on smartphones
explain: Fast Startup hibernates the kernel session instead of fully shutting down, which can block access to dual-boot volumes and cause some driver and wake issues.

q: What does Windows Startup Repair do when a PC will not boot?
options: It never succeeds at any repair and only displays a generic error message
It erases the entire drive and reinstalls Windows from the recovery image
It must be operated manually, one typed command at a time, by a technician
It attempts to automatically fix problems that prevent Windows from starting
explain: Startup Repair, run from the recovery environment, diagnoses and automatically repairs common boot problems such as damaged boot configuration.

q: Unusual outbound traffic suggests data is being copied off the network. What should this trigger?
options: Nothing, because outbound traffic is always safe
Incident response, treating it as possible data exfiltration
A routine increase in the backup schedule
A change of the office Wi-Fi password only
explain: Unexpected large or unusual outbound transfers are a sign of exfiltration and should start the incident response process for investigation and containment.

q: A device in Device Manager shows as disabled. How is it returned to use?
options: It can never be enabled again once disabled
It is enabled again from within Device Manager
It must be physically removed from the PC
Its driver package must be deleted first
explain: A disabled device, shown with a down-arrow icon, is simply re-enabled in Device Manager; it is often disabled accidentally or during troubleshooting.

q: Why should technicians document their findings when resolving significant issues?
options: Documentation is only useful for billing purposes
It replaces the need to actually fix problems
It builds a knowledge base that speeds up future troubleshooting
It is only required when a manager asks
explain: Written findings preserve symptoms, root cause, and the fix, creating a searchable knowledge base and a record for audits and handovers.

q: Why does hiding a Wi-Fi network's SSID provide little real security?
options: Because hiding the SSID encrypts all traffic using an outdated, weak cipher
Because the SSID can still be discovered and does not stop determined attackers
Because regulators in most countries require every SSID to be broadcast openly
Because a hidden SSID provides protection stronger than WPA3 encryption does
explain: A hidden SSID still appears in probe and association traffic and is easily found with basic tools; real protection comes from strong encryption and authentication.

q: A point-of-sale signature pad draws inaccurately and clicks register in the wrong place. What should be tried first?
options: Recalibrate the pad and check its driver
Assume the pad can never be repaired
Replace the pad immediately as defective
Reinstall the point-of-sale server software
explain: Calibration drift and driver problems commonly mimic hardware failure on signature pads, so recalibration and a driver check come before replacement.

q: A Windows service fails to start at boot. What should a technician examine?
options: Whether the desktop wallpaper loads correctly
The service's dependencies and the errors recorded in its logs
Whether the user's email client is open
The color depth configured for the display
explain: A service usually fails because a dependency did not start, its sign-on account has a problem, or a configuration error occurred; Event Viewer logs show which.

q: A 32-bit printer driver will not install on a 64-bit Windows system. What is the underlying issue?
options: The driver architecture must match the operating system architecture
32-bit drivers work on every system unchanged
The problem is always a faulty USB cable
Architecture makes no difference to driver installs
explain: Windows requires drivers built for the OS architecture, so a 64-bit system needs a 64-bit driver (with additional architecture drivers added on print servers for clients).

q: Task Manager shows disk usage pinned at 100 percent and the PC is very slow. What should be suspected?
options: A failing drive or a runaway process saturating the disk
A defragmentation is the only possible remedy
This is normal behavior for a healthy drive
A problem with the monitor's refresh rate
explain: Sustained 100 percent disk use points to a process flooding the disk or a hard drive that is failing and retrying reads; data should be backed up while it is diagnosed.

q: Which Windows tool provides a single console tree for Event Viewer, Disk Management, Services, and Device Manager?
options: Computer Management (compmgmt.msc)
System Configuration
Registry Editor
Windows Security
explain: Computer Management aggregates the core administrative snap-ins in one MMC console.

q: What does the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) allow an administrator to do?
options: Edit the Windows kernel directly from a console
Replace Group Policy with a single custom tool
Bypass User Account Control prompts entirely
Build custom consoles from snap-ins and save them for reuse
explain: The MMC is a host for administrative snap-ins; administrators assemble task-specific consoles and save them as .msc files for reuse.

q: What is the Startup tab in Task Manager used for?
options: Scheduling backup tasks and maintenance jobs to run at a specific time of day
Defragmenting and optimizing the system drive each time a user signs in
Enabling or disabling programs that launch at sign-in and viewing their startup impact
Managing the passwords, PINs, and sign-in options of local user accounts
explain: The Startup tab lists applications that run at sign-in, shows their measured startup impact, and lets an administrator disable them.

q: Which Task Manager view shows per-process CPU, memory, disk, and network usage in real time?
options: Services tab
Processes tab (with Details for the full list)
App history tab
Performance tab only
explain: The Processes and Details tabs expose live per-process resource consumption.

q: What are the three core Windows logs shown in Event Viewer?
options: Application, Security, and System
Setup, Forwarded Events, and Hardware
Admin, Operational, and Debug
Errors, Warnings, and Information
explain: Application, Security, and System are the classic core logs; Information, Warning, and Error are event levels recorded inside those logs, not log names.

q: A device in Device Manager displays a yellow exclamation mark. What does this indicate?
options: The device has been disabled by a user or by an administrator's policy
The device is operating normally and performing at its rated peak level
The device is a network printer that is currently being shared with others
The device has a problem, typically a driver issue shown in its status
explain: A yellow exclamation mark signals a problem state, most often a driver fault; a down arrow or red X indicates a disabled device instead.

q: Where is the option to roll back a device to its previous driver?
options: Disk Management, using the Action menu on the volume list page
Task Scheduler, using the Driver tab of a scheduled task item
Device Manager, in the device's Properties on the Driver tab
Registry Editor, by editing values under a generic Drivers key
explain: The Roll Back Driver button on the Driver tab of a device's Properties restores the previous driver package after a bad update, when a prior package exists.

q: How is the Windows Registry primarily organized?
options: As three plain text files stored together in the Windows system folder
Into five root hives such as HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE and HKEY_CURRENT_USER
As one single flat list of values with no grouping or hierarchy at all
Only as separate databases created individually for each user account
explain: The registry is organized under five root hives; HKLM holds machine-wide settings and HKCU holds the current user's settings.

q: Which registry hive contains settings that apply to the currently signed-in user?
options: HKEY_CURRENT_USER
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT
HKEY_USERS only
explain: HKCU maps the current user's portion of the profile; HKLM applies to the whole machine.

q: Why is editing the registry directly considered risky?
options: Each individual edit requires a new Windows product key before it can save
Making an edit automatically deletes the signed-in user's personal documents
Making an edit immediately disables the network adapter until the next reboot
Changes apply immediately with no undo, so an invalid change can break Windows
explain: Regedit saves changes as they are made with no confirmation or undo, so exporting a backup of the key before editing is standard practice.

q: What can an administrator control from the Services console (services.msc)?
options: The passwords and PINs belonging to local user accounts on the computer
The partition layout and drive letters of the system disk's volumes
Each service's startup type and whether it is started or stopped
The computer's BIOS passwords and firmware configuration settings
explain: Services.msc manages the start/stop state and startup type (Automatic, Manual, or Disabled) of Windows services, and shows their dependencies.

q: A service fails to start after the password of its log-on account was changed. Where is the correction made?
options: In the Disk Cleanup utility settings
In the service's Properties on the Log On tab
On the Boot tab of System Configuration
In the device's Properties in Device Manager
explain: The service stores its own copy of the log-on credentials, so the new password must be entered on the service's Log On tab before it will start.

q: For which task is System Configuration (msconfig) most useful?
options: Clean-boot troubleshooting by selectively disabling services and startup items
Formatting, partitioning, and assigning letters to the system disk
Creating, editing, and linking Group Policy objects to containers
Editing NTFS permissions and ownership on shared folders and files
explain: Msconfig's selective startup, together with hiding Microsoft services, lets a technician isolate which third-party service or startup item causes a problem.

q: Which Windows utility reports the DirectX version and display/sound driver details for troubleshooting games?
options: MSInfo32's Components page only
Disk Management
Credential Manager
DxDiag (DirectX Diagnostic Tool)
explain: DxDiag collects DirectX, display, and audio driver information commonly requested by game support.
