Chrome is permanently outdated on this PC and can no longer integrate with any registered antivirus scanner
explain: Chrome delegates download scanning to the registered antivirus, so a broken AV registration makes every scan fail.

q: When is wsreset.exe the standard fix to use?
options: When Windows will not boot and the recovery environment must be repaired first
When the Microsoft Store or its apps are stuck downloading or updating, because it clears the Store cache
When the printer is jammed and its queue must be reset from the command line
When Wi-Fi is slow and the network adapter cache must be cleared manually
explain: Wsreset clears the Microsoft Store cache without removing apps and then reopens the Store.

q: OneDrive shows red X sync errors on many files in a deep folder tree. What is a common hidden cause?
options: The full file path exceeds Windows path length limits, or filenames contain invalid characters
The files use colors that OneDrive cannot reproduce in its sync database
The user has too many monitors for OneDrive to track file changes reliably
OneDrive pauses sync on certain weekdays because of its service schedule
explain: Long paths and invalid characters such as < > : " | ? * break sync, and renaming or shortening the path fixes it.

q: OneDrive is stuck on 'Processing changes' for days. What is the documented reset procedure?
options: Format the drive so OneDrive can rebuild its local sync folder from scratch
Delete all cloud files so the sync engine has nothing left to process
Reinstall Windows to reset the OneDrive sync database and its registry keys
Close OneDrive and run %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset, then relaunch it
explain: The /reset switch rebuilds OneDrive's sync database state without deleting the user's files.

q: A user wants SharePoint or OneDrive files to free local space but stay visible in Explorer. How should they be set?
options: Set the files to Hidden so Explorer shows placeholders instead of contents
Set the files to Read-only so OneDrive stops downloading their contents locally
Set them to 'Free up space' (online-only) after confirming they are fully synced
Compress the files into ZIP archives stored inside the OneDrive folder locally
explain: Online-only placeholders keep the files visible in Explorer while reclaiming local disk space.

q: Teams and Zoom callers say a user's microphone sounds robotic and cuts out. Which Windows setting is a frequent culprit?
options: The webcam resolution selected for video calls in the meeting application
Audio enhancements, or an exclusive-mode or sample-rate mismatch, in the sound device properties
The meeting password, which limits audio quality for unverified participants
The user's desktop wallpaper, which the meeting app compresses with the audio
explain: Vendor audio enhancements and sample-rate conflicts garble VoIP audio, and disabling them is a standard fix.

q: A webcam shows 'Camera in use by another application' in Teams. How is this resolved?
options: Find and close the other app holding the camera, such as a browser tab or another meeting tool, and check privacy permissions
Buy a second webcam because Teams requires a dedicated camera device separate from other apps' camera use
Reinstall Windows to release the camera device lock that the other application holds across user sessions
Disable the microphone so the camera device is free to start streaming for the Teams meeting video feed
explain: Only one app can own most cameras at a time, and privacy settings can also block per-app camera access.

q: Screen sharing shows a black window when sharing a streaming app such as Netflix. What does this indicate?
options: A broken GPU that can no longer render protected streaming video content
A virus that blanks streaming windows whenever they are shared with others
A browser fault that requires reinstalling the browser to restore sharing
Expected DRM/HDCP behavior: protected video renders black to capture and sharing tools
explain: Content protection blanks protected playback in captures and screen shares, which is expected behavior rather than a fault.

q: Remote Desktop connects, then the session freezes within a minute. Which client-side fix often works?
options: Buy more RAM for the server first because RDP sessions freeze when the host runs low on available memory
Reinstall Windows on both ends to rebuild the Remote Desktop protocol stack and its transport components
Disable UDP transport for RDP in the client setting or policy, or update the network driver; MTU issues on VPNs are another suspect
Open port 3389 to the whole internet as a test and leave it open so NAT never interferes with the session
explain: UDP-based RDP transport interacts badly with some NAT and VPN paths, and forcing TCP is a known workaround.

q: A VPN client fails with error 809 when connecting to the office. What does this typically mean?
options: The user's VPN password is wrong and the server is silently rejecting the credentials before the tunnel forms
The VPN server is behind NAT and UDP 500/4500 traffic or the NAT-T registry setting needs attention, or the firewall blocks IPsec
The client's time is incorrect, so the IPsec certificates fail validation before the tunnel can be established
The VPN client needs its network profile recreated because its current tunnel configuration uses a legacy protocol
explain: Error 809 means the server did not respond, and NAT-T configuration and firewall rules for IPsec are the usual fixes.

q: An Excel workbook recalculates nothing and formulas show stale values until cells are edited. Which setting is responsible?
options: Calculation Options switched to Manual on the Formulas tab; set it back to Automatic
The file is read-only, which prevents formulas from recalculating their results
The screen is frozen, which pauses formula calculation until it is refreshed manually
The printer is offline, which blocks Excel from updating calculated values on screen
explain: Manual calculation, sometimes set by another workbook, leaves formula results stale until cells are edited.

q: A PDF prints garbled characters from one machine but prints fine from another. What is a reliable workaround?
options: Buy a new printer because the current one cannot render the PDF's embedded fonts
Convert the PDF to Word so the print driver receives editable text instead of glyphs
Ignore the garbled output because the printed text will correct itself on reprint
Print the PDF 'as image' from the reader, and update or reinstall that machine's print driver
explain: Printing as image rasterizes the page, which bypasses font and driver rendering faults on that machine.

q: Windows Fax and Scan or a legacy Java app is blocked after updates. What is the pragmatic help-desk approach?
options: Disable all future updates so the legacy components are never blocked again by security patch releases
Install the oldest Java version from a random download site to restore the legacy application immediately
Accept that legacy components are deprecated and migrate the workflow to modern scan apps and supported runtimes rather than weakening security
Turn off the firewall completely so the blocked legacy application can communicate without any restrictions
explain: Keeping unsupported platforms alive creates larger risks than migrating the workflow to supported tools.

q: Installing a desktop app fails with 'Windows Installer service could not be accessed.' What should be checked?
options: Format the drive so the Windows Installer service database is rebuilt cleanly
Confirm the Windows Installer service is not disabled, and re-register msiexec if needed
Replace the RAM because installer errors indicate failing memory during setup
Disable UAC permanently so the installer service can run without restrictions
explain: A disabled or corrupted Installer service breaks all MSI installs, and re-registering msiexec with /regserver repairs it.

q: An app worked yesterday but today crashes on launch for all users after a Windows update. What is the best-documented path?
options: Check the update's known issues and roll back the update or the app's recent patch; use Reliability Monitor to confirm the timeline
Delete every user profile because the update corrupted all of them at the same time across the computer
Reinstall Windows immediately before checking whether the update or the app's own patch is implicated
Replace the motherboard because a crash appearing after an update indicates a failing system board component
explain: Correlating the crash start with the update in Reliability Monitor points to the change that caused it.

q: A multi-user database program throws network errors only in multi-user mode. What does this pattern point to?
options: The client's monitor, which cannot display multi-user sessions correctly over the network
The client's keyboard, which sends malformed input in multi-user database sessions
The client's wallpaper, which the database server rejects during multi-user logons
The hosting and firewall configuration on the file server, where database service ports are blocked
explain: Multi-user accounting apps rely on a database service and specific ports on the host, which single-user mode bypasses.

q: Browser pages load but embedded videos never play after a driver update. What is a likely cause?
options: The monitor is too large for the browser to render embedded video content correctly
The site's videos were deleted at the same time the driver update was installed
A hardware acceleration conflict with the new GPU driver; toggle the browser's hardware acceleration to test
The browser's cookies expired, which prevents embedded video players from starting
explain: A broken GPU driver path breaks video decode and rendering in browsers, and software rendering isolates it.

q: A user installed a second antivirus 'for extra safety' and the PC became extremely slow with random freezes. What is the problem?
options: Viruses always cause this pattern whenever a second antivirus is present on a PC
Two real-time AV engines conflict through double scanning and driver contention; keep exactly one real-time AV
The PC needs more antivirus products to balance the scanning load between engines
The hard drive is too small to hold two antivirus definition databases at once
explain: Competing antivirus engines hook the same operations, while Defender steps aside for a single registered third-party AV.

q: Outlook rules stopped running after a mailbox migration. What is the typical fix?
options: Recreate or re-enable the rules, because rules tied to the old profile or store often do not survive migration
Recreate the Outlook profile first because the rules engine cannot run until a new profile is provisioned
Reinstall Windows to rebuild the Outlook rule engine, its profile settings, and the mailbox store indexes
Delete all email in the mailbox so the migrated rules have a clean set of folders to process messages into
explain: Client-side rules reference folders and stores that changed during migration, and rebuilding them restores automation.

q: A user's calendar shows meetings an hour off after traveling. What is the correct fix?
options: Delete all meetings and recreate them in the new time zone after traveling
Turn off daylight saving time permanently in Windows and the calendar app
Replace the CMOS battery first because it stores the calendar time zone offset
Set the correct time zone in Windows and in the calendar app's own time zone setting, because they can differ
explain: Outlook and web calendar apps have independent time zone settings, and a mismatch shifts displayed times while the data stays correct.

q: A shared OneDrive folder a user relied on 'disappeared' from Explorer and was replaced by an internet shortcut. What does this indicate?
options: A ransomware attack has encrypted the shared folder and replaced it with a shortcut for every collaborator
A disk failure deleted the shared folder's local sync database without warning the owner or collaborators
The folder's sharing was changed or the owner moved it; the .url shortcut links to the web location, so re-add the folder if it is still shared
A Windows bug removed the folder from Explorer even though its sharing and permissions never changed at all
explain: When sync of a shared folder stops because of permission or move changes, Explorer leaves a web shortcut in its place.

q: Google Drive or Dropbox created 'conflicted copy' files for a document edited on two machines. Why does this happen?
options: The file was infected on one machine, so the sync service preserved a quarantined copy
The same file was modified on both devices before either could sync, so both versions were preserved
The user typed too fast for the sync service to record the document's changes in order
The cloud service deleted the original maliciously and replaced it with conflicted copies
explain: Sync engines preserve both edits as conflicted copies rather than silently overwriting one version.

q: Windows Search finds files but Outlook items remain unsearchable. Beyond the index, what is an Outlook-specific check?
options: Ensure the Outlook profile's data files are included in indexing scope and the profile is not damaged; test in a new Outlook profile
The mailbox is in cached mode with a download window that excludes the recent messages being searched for
The email password length is preventing the search indexer from authenticating to the mailbox data file
The search catalog is stored on a drive that is nearly full, so new Outlook items cannot be indexed into it
explain: Indexing scope and profile health gate Outlook indexing independently of ordinary file search.

q: An application logs 'Access denied' writing to its own folder under Program Files. What is the modern fix?
options: Give Everyone Full Control on the entire Program Files folder so the application can write wherever it needs
Disable UAC permanently so applications can write to protected locations without ever triggering a prompt
Move Windows to another drive so the Program Files folder is no longer treated as a protected location
Redirect the app to write data to ProgramData or the user profile, granting targeted permissions only if the vendor requires it
explain: Applications should write data to ProgramData or AppData rather than Program Files, and loosening the whole tree is a security regression.

q: A legacy app shows tiny, blurry text on a 4K display while other apps look fine. What is the per-app fix?
options: Lower the whole display to 1080p so the legacy app matches other applications
Buy a magnifier to read the legacy app's unscaled text at native resolution
Use the Compatibility tab's high DPI settings and override scaling with 'System (Enhanced)'
Reinstall the display driver so the legacy app becomes DPI-aware automatically
explain: DPI-unaware apps can be scaled by the system with the Enhanced override instead of bitmap-stretching themselves.

q: Store apps for a single user are broken but work for other users. What is the likely fault?
options: The apps were uninstalled globally and only appear to work for other user accounts
That user's AppX registration or profile state; re-register apps for the user or rebuild the profile
The Microsoft Store is down worldwide and affecting this user first before others
The user's monitor is faulty and cannot render Store app windows correctly
explain: Per-user package registration corruption is profile-scoped, so re-registering packages or rebuilding the profile repairs it.

q: A scheduled backup application runs interactively but its scheduled jobs silently fail. What is a common cause?
options: The task runs under an account lacking 'Log on as a batch job' rights, or the stored password changed
The backup files are too large for Task Scheduler to start the job process reliably
The schedule falls on weekends, when Task Scheduler runs jobs with reduced rights
The monitor sleeps during the job, which cancels scheduled tasks without logging errors
explain: Batch logon rights and stale stored credentials are classic silent-failure causes for scheduled jobs.

q: A Linux user gets a graphical login loop: the correct password returns them to the login screen. What are the common causes?
options: A full home or root filesystem or broken permissions on ~/.Xauthority, or a crashed session; check disk space and logs from a TTY
The monitor is unplugged, so the desktop session cannot start after the user authenticates at the login screen
The password is too long for the graphical login manager to pass correctly to the desktop session starter
The kernel was updated, so every graphical login session crashes until the display manager is reinstalled fully
explain: Login loops classically trace to an unwritable home directory from a full disk or to session startup errors, revealed from a TTY.

q: After a package install on Debian or Ubuntu, apt reports broken dependencies. What is the standard repair?
options: Delete /var/lib/dpkg so apt can rebuild its package database from the installed files
Reinstall the operating system because broken dependencies cannot be repaired in place
Ignore all future updates so the broken dependency state is never triggered again
Run sudo apt --fix-broken install, then apt update and apt upgrade to complete the repair
explain: The --fix-broken option resolves half-configured packages and missing dependencies.

q: A Linux server's disk filled overnight because of logs. What is the journal-specific cleanup?
options: Remove the entire /var directory tree to reclaim all log space at once immediately
Disable all logging forever so the disk can never fill with log data again
Use journalctl --vacuum-time or --vacuum-size to trim the systemd journal, and review logrotate
Reboot weekly so temporary log files are cleared automatically by the init system
explain: The systemd journal can grow without bound, and its vacuum commands enforce retention limits.

q: On Linux, a newly copied script fails with 'Permission denied' when executed directly. What is the fix?
options: Rename the script with an .exe extension so the shell treats it as an executable program
Run chmod +x on the script, and ensure the filesystem is not mounted with the noexec option
Run the script as a different user whose account has a higher default umask setting applied
Delete the shebang line so the kernel executes the script with the default interpreter directly
explain: Copied files arrive without the execute bit, and chmod +x is the standard remedy.

q: SSH to a Linux host suddenly warns 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED.' After verifying the server was not compromised, what is the fix?
options: Remove the stale key with ssh-keygen -R <host> and re-accept the new host key on reconnect
Disable host key checking permanently for all hosts so the warning never appears again
Reinstall SSH on the client to rebuild its known_hosts database from all servers at once
Change your user password on the server because the host key is derived from it directly
explain: Rebuilt or re-addressed servers present new host keys, and the old known_hosts entry must be cleared after out-of-band verification.

q: A Linux workstation boots to an initramfs or busybox prompt. What does this usually indicate?
options: The graphical user interface has been disabled in the distribution's default boot target
The user has forgotten their password, so boot stops at the minimal initramfs shell prompt
The network is down, so the boot process cannot mount the root filesystem over NFS shares
The root filesystem could not be mounted, often fixed by running fsck on it from the prompt or live media
explain: Dropping to initramfs means early boot failed, frequently because filesystem corruption prevents mounting the root filesystem.

q: Wi-Fi disappears on a Linux laptop after a kernel update. What is a likely cause?
options: The router changed its own password by itself during the laptop's kernel update window
The battery is low, so the new kernel disables the Wi-Fi adapter to conserve power first
The out-of-tree Wi-Fi driver module (DKMS) failed to rebuild for the new kernel version
The screen brightness reset during the update, which also resets the wireless adapter state
explain: DKMS rebuild failures after kernel upgrades are the classic cause, fixed by reinstalling headers and the driver or booting the old kernel.

q: A Mac app downloaded from a vendor shows 'is damaged and can't be opened.' For a legitimately trusted app, what is usually the cause?
options: The Mac has a virus that has corrupted every downloaded application bundle stored in the user's Applications folder
Gatekeeper quarantine on a broken or unsigned bundle; re-download it, or remove the quarantine attribute (xattr) after verifying the source
The startup disk has failed and can no longer verify application bundle signatures or code requirements at launch
The app requires a newer Mac model because its bundle format is no longer supported by this version of macOS
explain: Damaged-app errors commonly trace to quarantine flags or corrupt downloads rather than actual damage to the app.

q: A Mac user is asked for a 'login keychain password' repeatedly after their account password was changed via an admin reset. What is the fix?
options: Update the keychain password to match, or create a fresh login keychain, because the keychain still uses the old password
Delete all passwords from iCloud so the local login keychain stops prompting for access
Reinstall macOS to synchronize the account password and keychain password automatically
Disable the keychain permanently so applications stop requesting stored credentials at sign-in
explain: Admin password resets do not change the keychain's own password, causing repeated prompts until they are resynchronized.

q: A Mac shows the spinning beachball for minutes whenever Finder opens a certain folder. Which causes should be investigated?
options: The desktop wallpaper image is too large for Finder to render at the same time as the folder's file previews
The keyboard needs cleaning because stuck keys are flooding Finder with repeated input events while it opens
The Mac is too old to open folders containing large media libraries without long preview generation delays
A huge folder of media generating previews, a failing drive, or a stuck network volume; test with a new folder and check Disk Utility
explain: Finder hangs usually trace to preview generation, failing disks, or unreachable network mounts.

q: AirDrop cannot see any devices though Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are on. Which setting should be checked?
options: The screen brightness, because AirDrop discovery dims when the display is set too low
The battery percentage, because AirDrop discovery stops below a fixed charge threshold
AirDrop discovery is set to Everyone, or Contacts Only with the contact present, and no VPN or firewall is blocking it
The Trash is emptied, because a full Trash prevents AirDrop from staging received files
explain: Discovery set to Receiving Off is the most common cause, followed by restrictive Contacts Only settings.

q: Time Machine reports 'backup disk not available' for a network backup. What should be checked?
options: Format the backup disk immediately so Time Machine can select it as a new target volume
Confirm the Mac is on the right network, the NAS or share is reachable, and re-select the disk in Time Machine settings
Delete all previous backups so the network share has room for a new full backup set
Turn off Wi-Fi so Time Machine is forced to rediscover the network backup disk at restart
explain: Network backup targets fail when the share moves or credentials change, so reachability and disk selection are checked first.

q: Safari will not load any sites though Chrome works on the same Mac. Where should troubleshooting focus?
options: Safari-specific state: clear website data, disable extensions, and check Safari's proxy and content blockers
The ISP, because a Safari-only failure indicates the provider is blocking its traffic specifically
The router, because it assigns Safari a different and broken network route than Chrome
The Mac's hardware, because Safari uses a network component that Chrome does not access
explain: Browser-specific failures point to browser-specific state, with extensions and cached website data leading the list.

q: Chromebook Android apps keep crashing after an update. What are the common fixes?
options: Powerwash the Chromebook immediately, because it is the only way to repair Android apps
Replace the Chromebook because its Android container cannot be updated after a crash loop
Disable the Play Store forever so the crashing Android apps can no longer be launched by users
Update ChromeOS and the Play Store components, clear the app's cache, or remove and reinstall the app
explain: Android container and app mismatches after updates usually yield to cache clears and component updates.

q: A Chromebook is slow with everything lagging. What is the most common real cause?
options: The battery is old and throttles the processor whenever the charge level drops below half
The screen is dirty and causes the touch and rendering layers to redraw the display repeatedly
Too many open tabs and extensions exhausting limited RAM; check the built-in task manager with Search+Esc
ChromeOS needs defragmenting because its files become fragmented like a Windows installation
explain: On low-RAM Chromebooks, tab and extension sprawl is the top performance complaint.

q: A user's ChromeOS profile shows 'profile error occurred' at sign-in. What is the typical resolution?
options: Replace the SSD because a profile error indicates the local storage device has failed permanently
Remove the user from the device and add them again, because their cloud data resyncs afterward
Call Google to delete the account so a replacement account can be created for the user instead
Enable developer mode so ChromeOS can repair the corrupted profile at the next sign-in attempt
explain: Corrupt local profiles are disposable on ChromeOS because everything meaningful lives in the cloud account.

q: What do Windows CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT blue screens point to?
options: A CPU core not responding: check overclocks, BIOS or firmware, chipset drivers, and CPU power and thermals
A printer jam that blocked a kernel thread waiting on the print spooler service queue
A full Recycle Bin that prevented the watchdog timer from writing its crash data to disk
A bad wallpaper that corrupted the display driver during the watchdog timeout interval
explain: This stop code means a processor failed to respond to an interrupt, so firmware, overclocking, and power are prime suspects.

q: What most often causes IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL blue screens?
options: The user's password expiring while a driver was processing a network logon request
The monitor cable carrying a signal that corrupts kernel memory access checks
Low disk space preventing the memory manager from paging data at the correct IRQL
A buggy, usually third-party, driver accessing paged memory at too high an IRQL
explain: This classic stop code points to drivers, and the minidump stack usually names the responsible .sys file.

q: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT blue screens direct the technician to check what first?
options: Replace the monitor because memory errors distort its display output during crashes
Reinstall all applications because one of them corrupted the memory manager settings
Test the RAM with Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86 and check recent driver changes
Defragment the disk because fragmented paging files trigger memory management errors
explain: As the name indicates, memory hardware or a driver corrupting memory is the first suspect for this stop code.

q: When does DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE typically occur?
options: When the battery is fully charged and the power driver refuses further charging input
When a device or driver mishandles a sleep or wake power transition; update the offending device's driver
When the user types too fast and the keyboard driver cannot keep its power state current
When the screen saver runs and changes the display driver's power state without warning
explain: Sleep and resume crashes with this code are driver power-management bugs.

q: What does VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE mean?
options: The GPU driver stopped responding and Windows' Timeout Detection and Recovery could not revive it
The monitor is unplugged, so Windows reports a timeout detecting the display device at boot
The video file is corrupt, so the media player reports a TDR failure to the operating system
The network dropped while streaming, so the video driver timed out waiting for frame data
explain: TDR failures suggest GPU driver instability, overheating, or failing graphics hardware.

q: To find which driver caused repeated blue screens, what should a technician enable and read?
options: The Reliability Monitor timeline, which shows crash dates but does not identify the faulting driver module
The Device Manager driver dates, which show update history but not which driver was running at the crash
The Event Viewer bugcheck entries, which record the stop code but not the driver stack that caused it
Small memory dumps in Startup and Recovery settings, then analyze them with WinDbg or WhoCrashed/BlueScreenView
explain: Minidumps preserve the crash stack, and viewer tools translate them into the likely culprit driver.

q: What is Driver Verifier (verifier.exe) used to do?
options: Verify Windows activation by checking driver signatures against the licensing service database
Update all drivers automatically to the latest versions published by their manufacturers
Stress-test drivers to provoke latent bugs into visible crashes that identify the bad driver
Check printer drivers only, because other driver classes cannot be verified by the tool
explain: Verifier deliberately pressures drivers, so it must be used carefully because it can make a machine unbootable until disabled in Safe Mode.

q: A game crashes with DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG after a GPU driver update. What is the standard remedy?
options: Buy a new monitor because the error indicates the display cannot keep up with the GPU
Clean-install the previous stable GPU driver, using Display Driver Uninstaller in Safe Mode for a full clean
Reinstall Windows first because driver remnants cannot be removed by any uninstaller tool
Disable the CPU's graphics scheduling so the game stops sending work to the hung device
explain: Corrupted driver remnants cause device-hung errors, and a clean rollback to a stable driver is the established cure.

q: CPU usage pegged at 100% by 'System Interrupts' suggests what problem?
options: A hardware device or its driver is flooding interrupts (DPC latency); update drivers and isolate the device
Too many desktop icons are forcing the kernel to process interrupt requests for each icon
A full Recycle Bin is generating interrupt requests whenever the shell refreshes its contents
The time zone is wrong, which desynchronizes the interrupt timer from the system clock source
explain: Interrupt storms are hardware or driver-level problems, and tools such as LatencyMon help identify the guilty driver.

q: A laptop throttles heavily even while plugged in and set to High Performance. Beyond thermals, what should be checked?
options: The wallpaper engine, because animated wallpapers reserve CPU performance in High Performance mode
The Recycle Bin, because a full bin forces the power manager to throttle background processing
The browser zoom level, because high zoom increases GPU load and triggers firmware throttling
The OEM performance mode in the vendor app or Fn key, and whether the correct-wattage adapter is in use
explain: Low-wattage adapters and quiet OEM modes cap performance despite the Windows power setting.

q: FPS in games dropped sharply right after a Windows feature update. What is the likely fix path?
options: Replace the GPU immediately because feature updates permanently reduce older cards' performance
Downgrade the monitor to a lower resolution model that the updated graphics stack supports
Update the GPU driver to a version supporting the new Windows build, and check Game Mode and fullscreen optimizations
Delete the games and reinstall them so they recompile for the new Windows feature build
explain: Feature updates change the graphics stack (WDDM), and matching GPU drivers usually restore performance.

q: One application slowly consumes more and more RAM until the PC bogs down. What is this behavior?
options: Normal behavior for all applications, which grow until Windows reclaims their memory at shutdown
A memory leak in the app; restart it for relief and update or patch it for the fix, confirming growth in Task Manager over time
A disk problem in which the paging file expands to match the application's working set growth
A network problem in which the app buffers received data in memory without ever releasing it
explain: Unbounded memory growth over hours is the signature of a leak, and only the vendor's fix is permanent.

q: Windows freezes completely at random intervals, requiring hard power-offs, with no blue screen. What are the prime suspects?
options: Failing storage, RAM errors, overheating, or PSU instability; check Reliability Monitor, temperatures, and drive health
The screensaver, which locks the display and input whenever it activates at random intervals
The mouse battery, which disconnects input and makes Windows appear completely frozen to the user
Too many browser bookmarks, which overload the shell when Windows indexes them in the background
explain: Hard hangs without a blue screen skew toward hardware, power, and thermal causes rather than a single driver.

q: A BSOD 'CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED' appears after a cleanup tool ran. What does this suggest?
options: The printer went offline during cleanup and a critical print process terminated unexpectedly
The battery died during cleanup, corrupting the critical process list stored in firmware memory
The Wi-Fi went down during cleanup, so a critical network process exited without reconnecting
Critical system files or registry entries were damaged; run DISM and SFC from WinRE and use System Restore if available
explain: Aggressive cleaner tools delete needed components, and image repair or System Restore is the recovery path.

q: What does BSOD 'BAD_SYSTEM_CONFIG_INFO' most directly implicate?
options: The GPU driver, which stores its configuration in a hive that failed to load at boot time
The network card, whose configuration was rejected by the kernel during driver initialization
Corrupt registry hives, often after a bad shutdown or disk issue; System Restore or a registry backup is the fix
The user's password, which is stored in a configuration hive that the logon process could not read
explain: This stop code reports that the system configuration in the registry is damaged.

q: A BSOD 'SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION' appears after installing new software. What does this usually mean?
options: The monitor failed at the same time the new software installed its display components
The new software installed a faulty driver or service; uninstall it or roll back via Safe Mode
The disk filled up during installation, leaving the new service without its working files
Windows needs activation because unactivated systems reject new kernel services at boot
explain: Timing plus this stop code points to a recently added kernel component misbehaving.

q: After enabling a Windows feature, installation fails with error 0x800f081f. What is the cause and fix?
options: The component source was not found because WSUS lacks it; point DISM or Group Policy to installation media or allow Windows Update as the source
The CPU is unsupported by the feature, so Windows setup hides its installation source files from the servicing stack
The feature requires a product key reactivation, so setup blocks installation until licensing is verified again
The system drive is encrypted, so setup cannot stage the feature's source files until the volume is unlocked
explain: Error 0x800f081f means source files were not found, a classic problem in WSUS-managed environments for Features on Demand.

q: Windows Update is stuck at 'Downloading 0%' for hours. Which quick remedies should be tried?
options: Format the drive so the update cache and download folders are recreated from a clean state
Buy a new PC because a stuck download indicates the update service hardware has failed
Disable the firewall permanently so update traffic is never inspected or delayed again
Check for a metered connection, restart the Windows Update and BITS services, and confirm free disk space
explain: Metered connections pause updates silently, and stuck services or a full disk are the other usual causes.

q: A feature update keeps failing and rolling back at the same percentage. Which built-in diagnostic tool is designed for this?
options: Disk Cleanup, which removes the failed update's files so the next attempt starts cleanly
The Snipping Tool, which captures the rollback screen code for support escalation tickets
SetupDiag, which analyzes setup logs to identify the blocking driver, app, or device
Task Manager, which shows which service consumed resources during the failed update attempt
explain: SetupDiag parses the Panther setup logs and reports the exact cause of a feature-update rollback.

q: A clean boot is helping diagnose a conflict. What is the efficient method to find the culprit?
options: Disable everything forever so the conflicting service can never run on the computer again
Use binary search: disable half the third-party services and startup items, retest, and narrow down
Enable items alphabetically so the conflicting service is found by its name order in the list
Reinstall Windows after testing each item so every result is measured on a clean system
explain: Halving the suspect set each round finds the culprit in a handful of reboots.

q: SFC reports it found corrupt files but 'was unable to fix some of them.' Where do the details live?
options: In CBS.log, searching for [SR] entries, after running DISM /RestoreHealth and SFC again
In the Recycle Bin, which holds the corrupt files that SFC removed during its repair pass
In the Photos app, which stores the screenshots SFC captured of each corrupt file it found
In the BIOS log, which records every file SFC verified during its pre-boot scan phase
explain: CBS logging records every SFC verify and repair operation for manual follow-up.

q: An app installs fine but Windows Sandbox fails to launch with a virtualization error. What is the fix?
options: Buy more RAM because Sandbox requires more memory than the error message reports needing
Disable the antivirus forever because it always blocks the Sandbox virtual machine from starting
Reinstall the app that failed, because its installer corrupted the Sandbox platform components
Enable virtualization in BIOS/UEFI and the Virtual Machine Platform and Windows Hypervisor Platform features
explain: Sandbox needs hardware virtualization exposed by firmware plus its platform features turned on.

q: WSL fails to start with error 0x80370102. What does this error mean?
options: The Linux user's password is wrong and WSL is refusing to start the distribution session
The disk is full, so WSL cannot create the virtual disk for the Linux distribution files
Virtualization is not enabled, because the BIOS setting and/or Virtual Machine Platform feature is missing
WSL has been discontinued, so current Windows builds return this error for every distribution
explain: Error 0x80370102 is WSL2's enable-virtualization error.

q: A Hyper-V VM has no network access after the host's NIC was replaced. What is the fix?
options: Reinstall the guest OS so it detects the host's new physical network adapter at setup time
Rebind the external virtual switch to the new physical adapter, or recreate the virtual switch
Disable the guest firewall because it is blocking the new adapter's network traffic by default
Change the VM's wallpaper because its network identity is tied to the guest desktop profile
explain: External virtual switches bind to a specific NIC, and replacing that NIC orphans the switch until it is rebound.

q: Quick Assist is the current Microsoft tool that replaced which earlier tool?
options: Windows Remote Assistance, for ad-hoc attended remote help with the helper's Microsoft account
Remote Desktop, which Quick Assist fully replaced for unattended server administration tasks
TeamViewer, which Microsoft officially replaced with Quick Assist for all commercial support
The Snipping Tool, whose screen-sharing features were moved into Quick Assist in recent builds
explain: Quick Assist is the built-in, Store-delivered successor to Windows Remote Assistance for helping another user interactively.

q: On Android, how does clearing an app's cache differ from clearing its data?
options: Clearing cache deletes the app itself, while clearing data only removes its downloaded updates
Clearing cache removes temporary files only, while clearing data resets the app completely, including accounts, settings, and databases
Clearing cache requires root access, while clearing data is available to any signed-in user account
Clearing cache clears the whole phone, while clearing data affects only the selected application
explain: Cache is cleared first for glitches, while clearing data is the stronger option that returns the app to first-run state.

q: An iPhone app keeps crashing after an update. How does 'Offload App' in storage settings help?
options: It removes the app binary but keeps its documents and data, then reinstalls a fresh copy of the app
It deletes the app and its data permanently so the user starts again with an empty install
It moves the app to iCloud forever so it runs from cloud storage instead of the device flash
It downgrades the app to the version installed before the update that introduced the crashes
explain: Offload and reinstall refreshes a corrupt app binary without losing the user's app data.

q: Android notifications for an important app arrive hours late. What is the usual cause?
options: The app is too old to use the current Android notification delivery service channels
The phone's clock is set incorrectly, delaying notifications until their scheduled times
The Wi-Fi channel is congested, so notification traffic is queued for hours by the router
Aggressive battery optimization, such as Doze or app standby, is deferring the app; exempt it in battery settings
explain: Battery managers restrict background work, and exempting the app restores timely notifications at some battery cost.

q: An iPhone user finds calls from unknown numbers go straight to voicemail. Which feature is likely responsible?
options: The carrier is blocking all calls from numbers that are not in the user's contact list
A broken speaker is preventing the ringtone from playing for unknown callers only
'Silence Unknown Callers' is enabled, or a Focus mode is filtering the notifications
Low Power Mode is silencing unknown callers to save battery during incoming calls
explain: Silence Unknown Callers sends non-contact callers to voicemail automatically, and users often enable it and forget.

q: RCS messages on Android are stuck on 'Setting up…' or fall back to SMS. What are the common fixes?
options: Buy a new SIM every time provisioning stalls, because RCS binds permanently to the first SIM
Update Carrier Services and the messages app, verify the number, and toggle RCS off and on, or clear the app's data
Turn off mobile data permanently so the messages app stops attempting RCS registration retries
Root the phone so RCS provisioning files can be edited directly in the system partition folders
explain: RCS provisioning glitches clear with component updates and a re-registration cycle.

q: iMessage activation fails with 'waiting for activation' for days. Which fix sequence should be followed?
options: Confirm the phone number and Apple ID are correct, date and time are automatic, carrier SMS works, and toggle iMessage off and on
Reinstall iOS immediately because a days-long activation failure always indicates a corrupt system
Replace the SIM as the only step, because activation depends entirely on a newly issued carrier SIM
Disable FaceTime forever because it competes with iMessage for the same activation token channel
explain: Activation depends on a silent carrier SMS and correct time, and toggling iMessage forces a retry.

q: Android shows a 'Moisture detected' warning and blocks charging after the phone got slightly damp. What is the correct handling?
options: Blow a hair dryer on hot directly into the port to evaporate the moisture as quickly as possible
Charge it anyway with force, overriding the warning repeatedly until the battery is full again
Put the phone in the freezer so condensation freezes and stops triggering the moisture sensor
Let the port dry fully and do not override repeatedly; persistent false alerts need the port cleaned or serviced
explain: The moisture sensor protects against shorts, and most cases clear after the port dries fully.

q: An iPhone displays 'Liquid detected in the Lightning connector' and refuses to charge. What should the user do?
options: Shake the phone hard to force water out through the speaker openings and connector pins
Use a metal pin to dry inside the connector by absorbing the liquid on its surface directly
Disconnect it and let it dry for several hours; an emergency override exists but risks damage
Charge wirelessly only forever, because a liquid alert permanently disables wired charging
explain: iOS blocks charging to prevent corrosion and shorts, and wireless charging can bridge the wait while it dries.

q: Auto-rotate stopped working on a phone after a drop, and rotation lock is off. What is a diagnostic step?
options: Reinstall all apps because one of them may have disabled the system rotation service globally
Check the accelerometer in a diagnostics or sensor app, because the sensor may be damaged
Blame the carrier and request a network reset, because rotation depends on carrier sensor data
Factory reset as the only test, because sensor faults cannot be checked any other diagnostic way
explain: Rotation depends on the accelerometer and gyroscope, and a sensor test isolates hardware damage after a drop.

q: One Bluetooth earbud is silent while the other plays. What are the common fixes?
options: Clean the mesh and contacts, check balance settings, and forget and re-pair the buds, resetting them in their case
Buy a new phone because single-bud audio indicates the Bluetooth radio has partially failed inside it
Replace the carrier SIM because earbud audio channels are assigned through the cellular profile
Turn off Wi-Fi because its signal always silences one earbud on dual-bud Bluetooth headsets
explain: Debris, balance sliders, and desynced bud pairing account for most one-sided earbud audio.

q: A phone's GPS places the user a block away in every app. How can accuracy be improved?
options: Turn off location services so apps stop using the inaccurate GPS position for directions
Use airplane mode so the GPS receiver works without interference from cellular radios
Delete the maps apps because they cache the inaccurate position between navigation sessions
Enable high-accuracy location with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning, and calibrate the compass with a figure-8 motion
explain: Assisted positioning from radios tightens location fixes, and magnetic interference throws the compass off.

q: Android alarms silently fail to fire for a user who relies on them. What is a leading cause?
options: The phone's alarm volume profile changes overnight because of its scheduled sound settings sync
Alarms need Wi-Fi to fire, so they fail silently whenever the overnight connection drops out
The clock app is battery-optimized as a 'sleeping app'; exempt it and check Do Not Disturb alarm settings
The ringtone is too quiet only, so the alarms fire correctly but are never heard by the user
explain: OEM sleep lists aggressively suspend clock apps, and exempting the clock app is the standard remedy.

q: An iPhone Screen Time passcode is forgotten. What is the supported recovery method?
options: Keep guessing the passcode until the device locks and offers a factory data recovery option
Reset it using the Apple ID credentials used when Screen Time was originally set up on the device
Restore from any backup file found online that contains a known Screen Time passcode value
There is no recovery method, so the phone must be replaced to regain Screen Time access
explain: Since iOS 13.4, the Screen Time passcode can be reset through Apple ID verification.

q: An Android phone is stuck in a boot loop after an update. Before a factory reset, what should be tried?
options: Wipe the cache partition from recovery mode, on models that support a separate cache wipe
Remove the battery while it loops, including on sealed phones, to force a clean power cycle
Flash a random ROM from a forum to replace the update that caused the boot loop condition
Keep it looping until the battery dies, then discard the phone as unrecoverable hardware
explain: A corrupt update cache causes many post-update loops, and a cache wipe is a non-destructive first step.

q: An iPhone is stuck on the Apple logo after an update. What is the correct first recovery step?
options: Start with a DFU restore immediately, because recovery mode cannot reinstall iOS in place
Let the battery die for a week so the update rolls back automatically when power returns
Shake the phone to reseat the storage connection that the update process loosened inside
Connect to a computer and use recovery mode to UPDATE, not Restore, iOS, preserving the user's data
explain: Recovery-mode Update reinstalls iOS while keeping data, and Restore with erasure is the fallback.

q: After a factory reset, an Android phone demands the previous owner's Google account. What is this?
options: A virus installed by the previous owner that locks the phone until their account signs in
A broken screen digitizer registering the account prompt as a false touch input repeatedly
Factory Reset Protection working as designed; only the prior account, or proof of purchase via the manufacturer or carrier, resolves it
An expired SIM preventing the phone from verifying ownership with the carrier's activation service
explain: FRP is a theft deterrent, and help desks must return the device to its owner or follow the OEM proof-of-purchase process.

q: An eSIM transfer to a new phone fails repeatedly. What is the correct resolution path?
options: Reuse the same QR code indefinitely until the carrier's system accepts the repeated activation attempts
Work with the carrier: they must issue a new eSIM activation or QR for the new device, because old QR codes are single-use
Transfer the physical SIM instead, because eSIM profiles can be copied onto a nano-SIM by the carrier store
Conclude it cannot be done, because eSIM profiles can never move between two different phone devices
explain: eSIM profiles are provisioned per device, so carriers re-issue activation when a transfer fails.

q: An Android work-profile user's camera is blocked 'by device policy,' while it works in their personal profile. What does this indicate?
options: Expected MDM policy behavior, not a fault; only the admin can change the work-profile restriction
A broken camera module that fails only when the work profile applications request access to it
A virus that targets managed work profiles by disabling their camera access through policy keys
A carrier issue in which the work profile's data plan blocks camera use on the managed network
explain: Managed profiles enforce restrictions per profile, so the help-desk answer is policy, escalated to the admin if it is wrong.

q: Google Play shows 'Download pending' for every app indefinitely. Which fixes should be tried?
options: Root the device so the Play Store download queue can be cleared from the system partition directly
Change the Google password daily until the stuck download queue accepts the new credentials
Disable the Play Store so pending downloads are cancelled and can never block new installs again
Cancel the stuck queue items, clear Play Store and Download Manager cache, and check available storage space
explain: A single stuck download blocks the whole queue, and clearing the Store cache restarts the pipeline.

q: An iOS update fails with 'Unable to Verify Update.' What is the common cure?
options: Restore the phone from a computer because unverifiable updates always indicate a corrupt iOS install
Turn off Wi-Fi forever so the phone stops downloading update packages it cannot verify locally
Delete the downloaded update in Storage and download it again on a stable network, and check storage space
Set the date back a year so the update's verification certificate falls inside its validity window again
explain: Corrupted update packages fail verification, and a fresh download on a stable network fixes most cases.

q: A user's Android phone in Safe Mode works perfectly, but crashes return in normal mode. What is the correct conclusion?
options: The hardware is faulty, because Safe Mode only masks intermittent hardware failures temporarily
A third-party app is causing the crashes; remove recently installed or updated applications to isolate it
Safe Mode fixed the problem permanently, so the crashes in normal mode must have a network cause
The carrier is at fault, because Safe Mode disables the carrier services that trigger the crashes
explain: Safe Mode disables third-party apps, so stability there isolates the fault to an app.

q: An Android phone will not exit Safe Mode after a reboot. What is a frequent cause?
options: A stuck volume-down button, often from a case pressing it, because Safe Mode is triggered by holding it during boot
A virus that reapplies Safe Mode at every boot by modifying the device's startup configuration files
An old battery that can no longer supply the voltage needed to boot into normal Android mode
A locked SIM that forces the phone into a restricted Safe Mode until the carrier unlocks it remotely
explain: Debris or a tight case holding Volume Down reapplies Safe Mode at every boot.

q: Voicemail notifications will not clear on an Android phone even with no messages. What is the fix?
options: Replace the phone because a stuck voicemail indicator indicates a failed notification controller chip
Delete all contacts because a corrupt contact entry is holding the voicemail indicator active
Turn off notifications permanently so the stuck voicemail indicator is no longer displayed to the user
Clear the Phone app's data or cache, or have the carrier reset the mailbox waiting indicator
explain: A stuck message waiting indicator clears with a Phone app data reset or a carrier-side mailbox reset.

q: A dual-SIM user finds data comes out of the wrong roaming SIM after travel. Which setting is responsible?
options: The APN is wrong for the home carrier, so data falls back to the roaming SIM's access point
The battery is failing, so the phone switches data to whichever SIM draws less power abroad
The default SIM for mobile data must be switched back in the SIM manager settings after travel
Wi-Fi is off, so the phone uses the last active SIM for all data until Wi-Fi is enabled again
explain: Phones remember per-function SIM defaults, and travel swaps often leave mobile data on the travel SIM.

q: Calls sound fine, but the other party cannot hear the user in one app while the phone app works. What should be checked?
options: The carrier tower serving the area, because app-specific microphone failures originate there first
That app's microphone permission, because it was likely denied or revoked in the app settings
The speaker, because a faulty speaker prevents the microphone from capturing the user's voice
The SIM tray, because a loose tray interrupts microphone audio for third-party calling apps only
explain: Per-app microphone permissions are the classic cause of a single-app audio failure.

q: A phone's screen brightness swings wildly indoors. What is the likely fix?
options: Clean the ambient light sensor area, often blocked by a case or screen protector, and reset adaptive brightness learning
Replace the display because wild brightness swings always indicate a failing backlight controller
Turn off the battery's adaptive charging so it stops interfering with the display brightness control
Reinstall the operating system to rebuild the adaptive brightness learning database from scratch
explain: Adaptive brightness learns from a sensor that needs a clear view, and cases or protectors are frequent blockers.

q: A tablet pen (stylus) stopped working after the tablet's update. Which checks should be performed?
options: Assume the tablet is dead because its pen digitizer stopped responding after the system update
Assume pens never survive updates and replace the pen without testing its battery or pairing
Check the Wi-Fi channel because pen input shares its radio band with the wireless network adapter
Re-pair or reconnect the pen, confirm its battery or charge, and check for a pen-specific driver or firmware update
explain: Active pens are Bluetooth and battery devices with their own update path, separate from the tablet's update.

q: A managed iPad says 'This iPad is supervised and managed by…' and the user cannot remove an app. What is the correct help-desk answer?
options: Walk the user through deleting the management profile so the app restriction is removed immediately
Tell the user to erase the iPad so supervision is removed and the app can be deleted afterward
Removal is restricted by the management profile by design; the user should contact the organization's IT department
The iPad must be jailbroken to fix a supervised device that will not allow an app to be removed
explain: Supervised devices restrict profile changes by design, and support should never coach a bypass of management.

q: A ChromeOS user's Linux apps suddenly will not launch after an update. What is a standard fix?
options: Buy a new Chromebook because its Linux container cannot be repaired after a ChromeOS update
Update the Linux container with apt update and upgrade inside it, or remove and re-enable the Linux feature
Enable developer mode so the Linux container can bypass the version check that blocks launching
Delete the user's account so a fresh profile recreates the Linux container in a working state
explain: Container and host version drift breaks Crostini apps until the container is refreshed.

q: Windows users report the company VPN connects but internal sites will not load, while home sites work. What is a prime suspect?
options: Split-tunnel routing or DNS: internal DNS servers are not being used for corporate names, a suffix or NRPT issue
The user's home router is too new, so it blocks corporate DNS suffixes from resolving correctly
The internal sites are down for everyone, including users who are working inside the office network
The VPN client needs a theme change because its current profile hides internal site traffic rules
explain: Name resolution is the usual split-tunnel failure: traffic routes, but DNS answers come from the wrong place.

q: An RDP user gets 'An internal error has occurred' immediately on connect. Which client-side fixes should be tried?
options: Open port 3389 wider on the firewall so the RDP client can negotiate its session without errors
Replace the server because an immediate internal error always indicates a failed remote host
Disable all RDP encryption so the client and server stop failing their security negotiation
Clear the RDP bitmap cache in the Terminal Server Client folder and reconnect, and also test NLA settings
explain: Corrupt client cache files are a well-known cause of instant RDP failures.

q: Outlook on the web works, but desktop Outlook says 'Trying to connect…' forever. What is a decisive test?
options: Reinstall Windows because desktop Outlook depends on system components the web version does not use
Replace the network cable because web Outlook tolerates cable faults that desktop Outlook cannot
Create a new Outlook profile; if it connects, the old profile or Autodiscover cache is corrupt
Delete the mailbox and recreate it so desktop Outlook receives a fresh Autodiscover configuration
explain: Profile corruption is the top cause of a one-client connection failure when web mail works.

q: A PDF form's fields are blank when opened on a phone, though the desktop shows entries. What is the explanation?
options: The file lost its form data when it was copied from the desktop computer to the phone for mobile viewing
The phone's basic PDF viewer does not render the form layer (XFA/AcroForm) the same way; open it in the full Acrobat app or flatten the form
The phone is infected with malware that hides PDF form field values from every viewer app installed on it
The form was saved without its field values embedded, so only the desktop's cached copy displays the entries
explain: Viewer capability differences, not data loss, explain blank fields, and flattening bakes the values into the page.

q: A user edits a shared Excel file and their changes never appear for others, with no errors. What should be checked?
options: Whether they are editing a local copy, from an email attachment or synced placeholder, rather than the shared cloud file
Whether Excel is broken globally, which would silently discard edits for every shared file user
Whether the file is too large for the sharing service to synchronize any further user changes
Whether the network is fine, in which case nothing is wrong and the changes will eventually appear
explain: Editing the wrong copy is the top silent collaboration failure, verified by checking the file's location in the title bar.

q: Browser-based email works, but the mail app on a phone stopped syncing after the user changed their password. What is the fix?
options: Assume the mail server is down because the phone app lost synchronization after the password change
Assume the phone needs a new SIM because its mail tokens are stored on the carrier SIM card
Assume email is being phased out on phones, so the app will not resume syncing after any change
Update the password in the account settings or remove and re-add the account, because the token was invalidated
explain: Password changes revoke app sessions, and re-authenticating the account restores sync.

q: A smart TV app crashes on launch after a TV software update. Which standard consumer fixes should be tried?
options: Replace the TV because app crashes after an update indicate its processor can no longer run apps
Call the ISP first because TV app crashes are usually caused by the internet connection profile
Power-cycle the TV fully by unplugging it for 60 seconds, update or reinstall the app, or check the vendor's status
Root the TV so the crashing app's cache and data folders can be cleared from the system partition
explain: Full power removal clears TV app caches that a remote-control 'off' does not clear.

q: A game console says NAT Type is 'Strict' and voice chat fails. What is the home-network fix?
options: Buy a second internet line dedicated to the console so its NAT type is no longer reported as Strict
Enable UPnP on the router or place the console in the router's DMZ or forward its ports, for one console only in DMZ
Turn off the router firewall entirely for all devices so console traffic is never filtered at home
Change the console's wallpaper because its network identity is rejected by the voice chat service
explain: Strict NAT blocks peer connections, and UPnP or port forwarding opens the needed paths.

q: A user's printer app on their phone finds no printers though the PC prints fine. What is the usual gap?
options: The phone is on a different network, such as guest Wi-Fi or a VPN, or the printer lacks mobile print support such as AirPrint or Mopria
The printer refuses phone jobs because its firmware prioritizes PC print queues over mobile apps
The phone needs a new battery because printer discovery requires full radio power to find devices
The PC is blocking the phone deliberately because it registered the printer as an exclusive device
explain: Printer discovery using mDNS does not cross network segments, so the phone and printer must share a LAN.

q: Windows dictation (Win+H) and voice typing do nothing when invoked. Which requirements should be checked?
options: A Kinect sensor must be connected because voice typing reuses its microphone array for speech recognition
A gaming headset must be used because standard microphones are not supported by the voice typing feature
Windows Pro is required because voice typing and dictation are not included in the Home edition feature set
A working microphone and an internet connection, because voice typing is cloud-powered, plus language support for the display language
explain: Voice typing processes speech online and only for supported languages, so it needs a microphone, connectivity, and a supported language.

q: A user reports their screenshots suddenly save to OneDrive instead of Pictures. What explains this?
options: A screenshot virus is redirecting saved captures to the user's OneDrive folder for exfiltration
A Snipping Tool update changed the default save location to OneDrive for all Windows users
OneDrive's folder backup (Known Folder Move) is capturing the Screenshots/Pictures folder; adjust it in OneDrive settings
A disk error corrupted the Pictures folder path, so Windows fell back to saving in OneDrive
explain: Known Folder Move redirects Pictures, including Screenshots, to OneDrive for many users.

q: A user double-clicks a .zip file and it opens in a photo app. What is the correct fix?
options: Reinstall Windows to restore every default file association to its original application at once
Rename the file to .exe so Windows opens it with its built-in archive extraction handler
Change the default app for .zip in Default apps settings, or via right-click Open with and Always
Delete the photo app so Windows is forced to choose a different program for ZIP files
explain: Broken associations are per-extension, and Open with > Always repairs the specific one quickly.

q: ZIP folders will not open at all and the extract option is missing after a third-party archiver was uninstalled. What is a fix?
options: Format the drive because the built-in ZIP handler cannot be restored after an archiver removes it
Re-register the built-in ZIP handling, or reinstall an archiver, because the uninstaller took the association and shell hooks with it
Buy a new PC because the shell extension database cannot be repaired on the current installation
Assume the files are gone because a missing extract option means the archives were deleted too
explain: Archivers register shell extensions, and sloppy uninstalls orphan them, so re-registering ZIP handling restores extraction.

q: Windows reports the Recycle Bin on C: is corrupted for every user after a disk error. What is the deeper check?
options: Run chkdsk on the volume, because recurring $Recycle.Bin corruption signals filesystem or disk problems
Ignore it forever because Recycle Bin corruption for every user has no underlying cause to investigate
Disable the Recycle Bin domain-wide so no user receives the corruption prompt on any computer
Reinstall all user profiles because each profile stores its own copy of the volume's recycle store
explain: One-off corruption is a folder fix, while recurring corruption points at the disk itself.

q: A specific program always opens maximized off-screen on a phantom third monitor. What is a registry-free alternative fix?
options: Delete the monitor driver so Windows forgets the phantom display's saved position data entirely
Reinstall Windows to clear every application's saved window position from the registry database
Discard the second monitor so the program is forced to open on the remaining physical display
Use Win+Shift+Left or Right arrow keys to move the focused window between displays until it is visible
explain: The Win+Shift+arrow shortcut moves the focused window across displays without editing the registry.

q: Microsoft Store apps open to a blank window and close after a few seconds for one user. Which repair often works?
options: Delete the user's documents because a corrupt document is crashing every Store app at launch
Replace the GPU because Store apps require hardware rendering that the current card fails
Clear the Store cache with wsreset and re-register the Store package for that affected user
Disable the internet because Store apps crash when they check for updates at launch time
explain: Per-user package state is again the fault domain, so cache clearing and package re-registration are the repair.

q: A user's Excel starts with a 'Personal.xlsb is locked for editing' prompt every time. What is the cause?
options: A virus is locking the personal macro workbook at every Excel startup for this user account
A leftover Excel process is holding the personal macro workbook; end it in Task Manager or delete the lock
The file is on a read-only network share forever, so Excel can never open it without prompting
Excel's license has expired, so it locks the personal workbook until the subscription is renewed
explain: Crashed Excel sessions leave the personal workbook locked by a ghost process.

q: Outlook takes 10 minutes showing 'Processing…' on the splash screen. What is a standard fix?
options: Start Outlook in Safe Mode (outlook /safe) to bypass add-ins, then disable the offending add-in; also try /resetnavpane for a corrupt navigation pane
Delete the OST and rebuild the profile, because a slow splash screen most often indicates a corrupt cached mailbox
Reinstall Windows to rebuild the Outlook splash screen, its profile loading components, and the mail store indexes
Buy a faster PC first, because splash screen delays of this length are caused by insufficient processor performance
explain: Splash hangs are add-in and profile territory; /safe isolates add-ins and /resetnavpane repairs a classic corruption.

q: A user cannot send email from Outlook and messages sit in the Outbox. Beyond connectivity, what should be checked?
options: The monitor's brightness, because a dimmed display hides the Send progress dialog from the user
The user's signature font, because an unsupported font can block the entire Outbox send queue
The Recycle Bin, because deleted sent items can back up into the Outbox and block new messages
Whether an oversized attachment is wedged at the top of the Outbox, and that the account's outgoing server settings are correct
explain: One huge stuck message blocks the queue behind it, and Work Offline lets the user remove it.

q: A shared mailbox does not automap in Outlook after being granted access yesterday. What is the mundane explanation?
options: The shared mailbox has been deleted, so automapping has no target mailbox left to add to the user's folder pane
Outlook is broken and must be reinstalled before any newly granted shared mailbox can appear in the folder pane
Automapping and permission propagation can take time and an Outlook restart; Full Access automaps, while Send As alone does not
The network is down, which prevents Exchange from delivering the automapping configuration to the user's Outlook
explain: Exchange permissions propagate on their own schedule, and a restart plus patience usually completes automapping.

q: Windows shows 'We can't sign in to your account' and loads a temporary profile after an update. What is the profile-repair step?
options: Delete the user's files in the temporary profile so the original profile is forced to load next time
Check the ProfileList registry keys for a .bak entry and restore the correct profile path, after backing up the registry
Reinstall every application because a temporary profile means all app registrations were lost in the update
Ignore it because temporary profiles are permanent once Windows loads one after an update failure
explain: The .bak ProfileList mix-up is the textbook cause, and correcting the entries reunites the user with their profile.

q: A PC's fans spin up when idle and Task Manager shows 'System Idle Process' at 99%. What should the user be told?
options: That is normal: the System Idle Process percentage is time the CPU is doing nothing at all
Their CPU is failing and reporting idle time incorrectly whenever its fans spin up at idle
A virus is necessarily mining at idle and using the Idle Process entry to hide its activity
Windows should be reinstalled because the Idle Process should never appear in Task Manager
explain: The Idle Process is accounting for free CPU time, not a workload, which is a classic user misconception.

q: One drive letter vanished from Explorer though Disk Management shows the volume healthy. What is the quick check?
options: Format the volume so Explorer assigns it a fresh drive letter during the new filesystem creation
Replace the drive because a healthy volume that hides its letter indicates a failing controller board
Reinstall Explorer because it has lost the volume's letter from its shell namespace registration cache
Check whether the drive letter was removed, and reassign it in Disk Management, or whether a policy or setting hides the drive
explain: Healthy but invisible volumes usually lost their letter or are hidden by the NoDrives setting.

q: A user's OneDrive icon vanished from the tray and sync stopped silently. How is it restarted?
options: Reinstall Windows to restore the OneDrive tray icon and its startup registration entries completely
Delete the cloud files so OneDrive restarts itself to resynchronize an empty account folder set
Run OneDrive.exe from %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive and check its startup entry in Task Manager
Format the drive so OneDrive's local cache and icon registration are rebuilt from a clean state
explain: OneDrive can exit or lose its autostart entry after updates, and relaunching it restores sync.

q: A corporate app fails only when the VPN is connected and works fine in the office. What does this pattern implicate?
options: The app is incompatible with home networks and fails whenever it detects a residential IP address
The VPN's DNS or routing for that app's servers, such as a split tunnel missing a route, or MTU; not the app itself
The user's home PC is too old to run the app correctly while a VPN tunnel is also established
The app vendor's branding causes the VPN client to deprioritize its traffic on home connections
explain: A location-dependent failure is a path-dependent failure, and the tunnel configuration is the variable that changed.

q: Teams shows the user as 'Unknown user' and presence is not updating. What is a known fix?
options: Clear the Teams cache and sign out and back in; new Teams stores its cache under its package folder
Reinstall Windows to rebuild the Teams identity and presence registration for the user account
Replace the webcam because Teams derives presence identity from the connected camera device
Call the carrier because presence updates are delivered through the mobile carrier's network
explain: Presence and identity glitches in Teams are usually stale local cache.

q: The default browser keeps reverting to Edge after every update for one user. Beyond user choice, what should be checked?
options: The user's wallpaper, because Edge resets browser defaults when it detects a non-Microsoft image
The mouse settings, because a misconfigured click can reapply Edge as the default at logon time
The time zone, because browser defaults are scheduled to reset when the zone changes after updates
Whether a policy such as GPO or MDM, or a 'browser protection' utility, is enforcing the default browser
explain: Managed defaults come from policy or guard software that reapplies them after updates.

q: A user gets 'The file is open in another program' for a local document no one else uses. Who often holds the file?
options: A coworker connected remotely who left the document open in a background terminal session overnight
The Recycle Bin, which locks deleted copies of the document that share its name and folder path
The Explorer preview pane, or a crashed app instance, locking the file; close the preview or the app process
The printer, which locks documents it has spooled until their print jobs finish or are cancelled fully
explain: Preview handlers lock files while rendering them, and disabling the preview pane or ending the process releases them.

q: Fonts appear jagged in Windows for one user after they 'optimized' settings. How is this restored?
options: Reinstall all fonts on the system because the optimization deleted their smoothing hinting data
Use the ClearType Text Tuner (cttune) and enable the performance option 'Smooth edges of screen fonts'
Buy a new GPU because jagged fonts after a settings change indicate failing text rendering hardware
Lower the resolution to minimum so jagged font edges are no longer visible at the reduced size
explain: Users disable font smoothing in performance tweaks, and ClearType recalibrates rendering.

q: The Windows key and taskbar shortcuts stop working while games run fine. What is a likely suspect?
options: The keyboard's 'game mode' or a stuck Win-Lock key is disabling the Windows key during play
Windows has been deactivated, which disables the Windows key and taskbar shortcuts in games
The GPU driver is intercepting Windows key shortcuts to reserve them for its overlay features
The game is a virus that disables the Windows key to prevent the user from leaving the session
explain: Gaming keyboards have a Windows-key lock that is easy to trigger accidentally.

q: A user's second monitor works in Windows but the login screen appears only on the closed laptop lid. What should be set?
options: Set a BIOS password so the firmware displays the sign-in screen on all connected monitors equally
Set the screensaver to start before sign-in so the login prompt moves to the external display first
Create a new user account whose sign-in screen defaults to the external monitor instead of the lid
Set the external display as the main display, or duplicate the screens, so sign-in shows where the user looks
explain: The sign-in screen follows the primary display designation, so the external display must be made primary or duplicated.

q: Battery drains fast on a sleeping Windows laptop with modern standby drain. How is this diagnosed?
options: Check the battery health report, which shows capacity loss but not which activators kept the system awake
Check Task Manager's startup list, because a heavy startup app is draining the battery before standby begins
Run powercfg /sleepstudy to see what kept the system active during the standby period in question
Check the network adapter's power settings, because its wake timers are the only activators SleepStudy reports
explain: SleepStudy reports the activators, such as network, devices, and apps, behind standby battery drain.

q: Windows Hello works, but after undocking, face sign-in fails until reboot. What is a likely cause?
options: The user's face changed enough while docked that Hello no longer recognizes it after undocking
The dock's USB camera or IR path, or a second camera, is confusing Hello; set the correct camera or restart the biometric service
The TPM is full, so Hello cannot store another face template while the laptop is undocked at logon
The Wi-Fi dropped during undocking, which prevents Hello from verifying the face template online
explain: Multiple cameras, such as a lid IR camera plus a dock webcam, confuse Hello's device selection.

q: An Excel add-in tab vanished after an Office update. What is the correct fix?
options: Re-enable the add-in under Add-ins options, checking Disabled Items first for a crashed add-in
Reinstall Windows to restore the Office add-in registry entries removed by the feature update
Delete the workbook that used the add-in because its ribbon customization stored the missing tab
Buy a new Office license because updates remove add-in tabs from unlicensed installations only
explain: Crashes move add-ins to Disabled Items, where they must be explicitly re-enabled before use.

q: Word documents open in Protected View from the local file server, annoying users. What is the correct admin fix?
options: Turn off Protected View for everything so documents from any source open in full editing mode
Tell users to ignore Protected View because it cannot be changed for file server locations at all
Move the documents to USB drives so Word treats them as local files outside Protected View scope
Add the file server's location to Trusted Locations or trusted sites rather than disabling Protected View globally
explain: The source location should be trusted specifically, rather than disabling Protected View for the whole surface.

q: A user renamed their PC and now a mapped application that referenced the old name fails. What is the lesson and fix?
options: Renaming PCs is impossible without breaking applications, so the old name must be restored forever
The application is corrupt and must be repaired because it stored the old PC name in its program files
Update the app's server reference to the new name, or use a DNS alias; shortcuts and configs using the old hostname broke
Reinstall the app on every PC so each installation learns the renamed computer's new hostname value
explain: Name-based references break on renames, and DNS aliases prevent recurrence.

q: After editing /etc/fstab badly, a Linux system boots to emergency mode. What is the correct fix path?
options: Reinstall Linux immediately because a bad fstab entry cannot be edited from the emergency shell
Use the emergency shell to remount root read-write, correct or comment the bad fstab line, and reboot
Delete /etc/fstab entirely so the boot process mounts filesystems with its built-in defaults only
Buy a new drive because emergency mode indicates the edited fstab corrupted the disk's partition table
explain: A bad fstab entry halts boot, and emergency mode exists precisely to allow this repair.

q: Which of the following correctly completes this statement: "Linux: a service fails at boot with 'address already in use.' The diagnostic is ____"?
options: ss -tulpn (or netstat) to find which process already holds the port
An app or process using the drive (Finder previews, Spotlight indexing, an open file); check with lsof or quit the app
Reset NVRAM and the SMC (Intel) / restart (Apple silicon), and check System Information for the Wi-Fi interface
Signature mismatch: the new APK is signed with a different key than the installed app (uninstall first, losing data)
explain: Port conflicts are resolved by identifying the squatter process, not by blind restarts.

q: Which of the following correctly completes this statement: "macOS: an external drive 'cannot be unmounted' when ejecting. The usual holder is ____"?
